# Issue #1154: One Shell-Argument Reading for the Whole Agentic Module

Issue [#1154](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1154) (E119):
Codex's shell tool `exec_command` sends the command under the argument key
`cmd`, while `progress.rs` read only `command`. The work-item read was never
recorded as attempted, and the stateless planner re-derived the identical
`gh issue view` call 78 times in a row (6.2M input tokens) until the client
compacted the thread. The full incident account, with the transcript excerpts,
is `docs/case-studies/issue-1154/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1154-1 | One shared `command_argument` for the whole `agentic_coding` module, reading the argument key from the client's declared tool schema (the key whose schema describes the shell command), falling back to `command`, `cmd`, `script`, and an array form joined for `shell`-style tools; the seven local copies are deleted. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` holds the one shared `command_argument` (string and joined-array forms, `command` → `cmd` → `script`), and the seven former copies in `progress.rs`, `file_read.rs`, `tool_result.rs`, `narration.rs`, `command_reroute.rs`, `evidence_record.rs` and `workspace_change.rs` delegate to it (JS twin `commandArgument` in `js/agentic/tool_result.mjs`). The schema reading is wired since 2026-10-07: `command_argument_key` resolves the property whose own schema describes the shell command (never the working-directory property), and `project_declared_command_keys` (JS `projectDeclaredCommandKeys`) projects the request's tool definitions onto the transcript before planning, so a call whose tool declares its command under another key (e.g. `shell_command`) carries that value under `command`; the projection is pure (no state between requests, client messages untouched) and runs at both servers' agentic entry (`agentic_outcome` in `rust/src/protocol.rs`, `agenticOutcome` in `js/server/agentic.mjs`). Pinned by `the_command_key_is_read_from_the_tool_schema` and `a_schema_declared_key_plans_exactly_as_the_command_key` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` (drafted without a local cargo run) and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs` (8 tests passing locally, including the server entry). |
| R1154-2 | Invariant independent of parsing: never plan a tool call whose name and arguments are byte-identical to one already attempted in the current turn window; if the planner would, report the stuck step and its last result instead of repeating it. | Implemented: `Progress::repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`, JS `Progress.repeatedCall` in `js/agentic/progress.mjs`) recognizes a completed call by byte-identical arguments or the same canonical command/URL operand (the protocol layer may project `command` onto `cmd` before the transcript echoes the call), and `stop_repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`, JS `stopRepeatedCall`) replaces the repeat with the `stuck_step_report` answer from `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. A completed call is the loop signature; a failed one keeps its existing bounded retry and the two-failure stop of issue #1133. Pinned by `repeated_successful_read_is_reported_not_replanned` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` and by the R1154-2 cases of `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs`. |
| R1154-3 | After a successful read, the fetched text drives `plan_work_item_execution` exactly as on the Claude and Agent paths. | Implemented by the shared reading: `issue_view_url` resolves under `cmd` (and under a schema-declared key through R1154-1's projection), the read lands in `fetched_pages`, and `repository_work_item_objective` feeds `plan_work_item_execution` unchanged. Pinned by `codex_cmd_read_drives_execution_instead_of_repeating` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs` and its JS twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1154-command-argument.test.mjs`. |
| R1154-4 | Tests: replay the Codex transcript's first two Responses items (`function_call` `exec_command {"cmd": …}` + `function_call_output`) through the Responses input conversion and assert the next plan is not another `gh issue view`; a table test over `{command}`, `{cmd}`, `{script}`, `{command:[…]}` yields the same recorded read. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs`: the replay goes through `ResponsesRequest::to_chat_completion_request` (the server's own conversion), and the table covers all four spellings plus the twice-repeated transcript shape. |

# Issue #1155: Work-Item Read Validation and Honest Fallbacks

Issue [#1155](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1155) (E120):
an unauthenticated `gh issue view` printed its how-to-authenticate banner, the
Agent CLI echoed that output with the exit status dropped (`"metadata":
{"exit": 4}` in its own record, plain text in the tool message Formal AI
received), and the banner was accepted as the issue body. The run then wrote
`.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and answered `planned_not_executed`
without ever trying the `webfetch` tool the client offered. The full account,
with the transcript excerpts, is `docs/case-studies/issue-1155/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1155-1 | The read observes its own status whatever the client sends: the planned read ends with `printf '\n__formal_ai_exit=%s\n' $?`, as data in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (`issue_view_command`), and a non-zero status is a failed read. | Implemented: `issue_view_command` in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (and the byte-identical embedded mirror) now appends the sentinel `printf`; `exit_sentinel` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`) reads the last `__formal_ai_exit=N` line and `work_item_read_failure_reason` turns any non-zero status into a failed read even when the client's echo carries no error flag. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): the twins in `js/agentic/progress.mjs` and `js/agentic/general_execution.mjs` behave the same, and `composeRepositoryWorkPlan` (`js/agentic/general_planner.mjs`) now accepts an objective that opens with the work-item reference, as the Rust `opens_with_reference` does; without it the JavaScript planner never reached the read and fetched the issue page through the generic capability route instead. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1155-read-validation.test.mjs`. |
| R1155-2 | The read's shape is validated before it is accepted as the issue: a title line, a blank separator, then the body — output without that shape is a failed read, recorded with its text. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_reason` requires the `gh` reads to contain the blank-line separator (the incident banner has none) and the raw-body `curl` read to be non-empty text that does not begin like the API's JSON error blob; failed reads land in `Progress::failed_work_item_reads` with their reason and are never pushed to `fetched_pages`. Pinned by `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` and `a_failing_sentinel_outranks_a_well_shaped_output`. Pinned in both roots by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1155-read-validation.test.mjs`. |
| R1155-3 | On a failed read, walk the fallbacks in order and record each attempt: the client's fetch tool on the issue URL, `curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/<issues|pulls>/<n>`, `gh api`, then the prepared PR's title and body. | Implemented: `plan_work_item_read` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/general_execution.rs`) now plans, after the failed `gh` view: the fetch tool on the issue URL, `issue_rest_read_command` (credential-free `curl` with the raw-body `Accept` header), `issue_api_read_command` (two `gh api` calls printing title and body), and last `prepared_pull_reference` — the pull request the prompt names, fetched as page context. Pull-request work items read their REST `pulls/` endpoint. Every attempt is recorded; `Progress::work_item_read_attempts` lists them. Pinned by `the_rest_routes_follow_the_fetch_fallback_in_order`, `the_rest_fallback_of_a_pull_request_reads_the_pulls_endpoint`, `the_prepared_pull_request_is_the_last_read_fallback`. Pinned in both roots by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1155-read-validation.test.mjs`. |
| R1155-4 | Only when all routes fail is `planned_not_executed` honest: the answer lists every read tried with its result, and the only write is never spent on the plan record when the goal could not be read. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_report` (filled from the `read_failed_report` data key) closes the run with every read, its reason and its first answer line — and `general_change_step` returns it before the `PLAN_PATH` write, so no plan record is written for an issue the session never read. Pinned by `an_exhausted_retrieval_reports_every_read_and_writes_no_plan_record`. Pinned in both roots by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1155-read-validation.test.mjs`. |
| R1155-5 | Replay test from the transcript: with the Agent tool list (`webfetch`) and the `gh` result without exit status, the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL; with the sentinel line `__formal_ai_exit=4` the read is a failure. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` (the file name the dispatch directed; the issue's Definition of Done names `issue_1155_work_item_read_failure.rs` — same tests, rename at registration if preferred): `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` replays the status-less echo, `with_the_sentinel_line_the_read_is_a_failure_and_the_fetch_follows` replays it with `__formal_ai_exit=4`, and both assert the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL. |

Residuals for the main session: `REQUIREMENTS.md` and
`docs/requirements-traceability.md` regeneration
(`rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`) and the
released-version manual confirmation row of the issue's Definition of Done.
The unit file is registered in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`. Both ledger copies of
`data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` were edited byte-identically (the data/meta
tree is nominally main's; the issue requires the sentinel and the fallback
wording to live there as data).

## Issue #1156: Single output obligations

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1156

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Repeated identical quoted stdout requirements are deduplicated in first-mention order; distinct output operands retain their order. The generated output verifier therefore compares against the composed single obligation. Workflows use the recipe artifact stem rather than a shared run.yml path. | Drafted. Inline regressions cover duplicate and distinct output requirements. Existing output-verifier template already uses byte comparison and propagates process failure. No local execution was performed. Repository/task-specific workflow naming beyond artifact stems remains open. |

## Issue #1157: Idempotent recipe commits

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1157

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Recipe commits stage only declared artifacts and inspect the cached diff restricted to those paths. No-change runs emit __formal_ai_commit_unchanged, then still push and print the current hash. Continuations consume the planner evidence window, retaining already completed writes and commands. | Partial. Idempotent commit and continuation replay are drafted. Output ignore patterns and verification of artifacts after externally modified continuation state remain open. No local builds or tests were run. |

## Issue #1158: Pull request completion and feedback

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1158

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | After a verified recipe commit, PR targets retrieve comments and reviews, update their description from artifact and verification commands, and mark draft PRs ready only with a clean working tree. Already-ready PRs are accepted. Nonempty comments, requested changes, or unreadable feedback block readiness with the observed feedback. | Partial. Feedback retrieval, description editing and guarded readiness are drafted. Deriving and applying arbitrary review-requested source edits remains open; feedback is never represented as resolved merely because it was fetched. |

## Issue #1159: Workspace prerequisite recovery

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1159

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Run failures are classified with the shared prerequisite classifier. Missing executables with FORMAL_AI_INSTALL_GRANT=workspace fetch their pinned publisher. A public process-free parser accepts only typed setup notation with a postcondition. Harness tools execute scoped setup, postcondition and one original-command retry, with explicit PATH and transcript binding; absolute/parent write scopes and shell/escalation setup programs are refused. | Partial. Typed publisher recovery is drafted and bounded. Ordinary publisher prose cannot become an executable recipe. Broader source discovery, per-process/network grants and typed recipes for publisher pages that lack them remain open. No local process installation, build or test was executed. |

Applying arbitrary reviewer source changes and deriving substantive verification commands from restart context remain open. No builds/tests or pushes were performed. |

## Issue #1161 Client Registry Names the Agent Config Env

Issue [#1161](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1161) (E126)
makes the client registry declare *how* a client is pointed at its config —
the env var that relocates it — instead of implying an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
relocation that also moves `gh`'s and git's config and breaks GitHub
authentication inside the session. The incident analysis, the per-client
evidence, and the fix live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1161/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1161-1 | Every `global_configs` entry in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` can declare the environment variables that relocate its own config file (`config_env "VAR"` children), parsed into a new `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig::config_env: Vec<String>`; entries whose file has no relocation variable declare an empty list. | Implemented: the `config_env` field and parser arm in `rust/src/seed/client_integrations.rs`, filled in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` (and its committed `rust/embedded/` mirror) only where in-repo evidence exists. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_env.rs`. |
| R1161-2 | `agent` names `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` (config file) and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (directory); `codex` and the `t3code` OpenAI-protocol entry name `CODEX_HOME`; `opencode`, `opencode-vscode` and `opencode-desktop` name `OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. | Implemented in the same seed file. Evidence per client: agent — the issue itself and the wrapper's own `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_CONTENT` one-shot mechanism; codex — `docs/configuration/output-sessions.md` (`$CODEX_HOME/sessions/…`), `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/README.md` (`CODEX_HOME` → a directory holding `config.toml`) and `rust/tests/issue_760.rs`; t3code — its own ephemeral block relocates the same `config.toml` via `CODEX_HOME` (`docs/configuration/t3-code.md`); opencode family — each block's own ephemeral `config_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG"` / `config_dir_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR"`. Pinned by the per-client assertions in the same test file. |
| R1161-3 | The declaration is a registry surface: `formal-ai clients --format json` carries it additively as `global_configs[].config_env` (plus the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` top-level fields), and `formal-ai clients` prints it on each `global[...]` line. | Implemented in `rust/src/cli_clients.rs` and tested against the built binary: `rust/tests/integration/issue_1161_clients_surface.rs` runs `formal-ai clients --format json` and asserts, for every seeded client, that each `global_configs[].config_env` and the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` fields equal the parsed seed and that `verification.surface` is still present (`clients_json_carries_each_global_config_relocation_variable`), and runs `formal-ai clients` and asserts each client's `global[...]` line ends with ` via <variables>` exactly when it declares some (`clients_text_prints_the_relocation_variables_on_each_global_line`). Additive only — the matrix (`experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh`) still reads exactly the `verification.*` fields it read before. |
| R1161-4 | A host integration contract is documented: a host that needs a task-local client config sets the declared variable and must not relocate `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` (the 2026-09-27 `gh`-auth incident, link-assistant/hive-mind#2314). | Implemented: the "Host integration contract" section and the *Relocate via* column in `docs/configuration/agentic-clis.md`, the registry-surface note in `docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1161-host-contract.test.mjs`, which reads the declared variables from `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` and asserts that the contract's bullet for each declaring client names every one of its variables, that the clients declaring none are named as such, that the *Relocate via* column lists every declared variable, and that the section forbids relocating `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` and cites link-assistant/hive-mind#2314. |
| R1161-5 | Clients whose global entry is a shell profile (`gemini`, `claude`, `qwen`, `aider`) or a fixed path with no evidenced variable (`cursor`, `grok`) declare none; no variable is fabricated. | Implemented and pinned by `entries_without_a_relocation_variable_declare_none` in the same test file. |
| R1161-6 | Hive Mind switches its Formal AI agent launcher from the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` relocation to `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`/`LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG`. | Implemented in Hive Mind and confirmed from this repository on 2026-10-07: link-assistant/hive-mind commit de14357623 ("fix(#2314): keep gh authenticated in the Formal AI tool env", 2026-09-27) makes `buildFormalAiClientEnv` in `src/formal-ai-runtime.lib.mjs` set `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (agent) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (opencode) to the directory of the registry's `global_configs[].path` instead of relocating `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, with the regression test `tests/formal-ai-tool-env-keeps-gh-auth-2314.test.mjs`; hive-mind#2314 closed as completed on 2026-09-28, and the commit is an ancestor of the hive-mind release v2.33.14. This repository's side of the contract — a JSON global config that declares that `*_DIR` variable for each client the launcher maps, and no client declaring `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` — is pinned by `R1161-6: every JSON-configured client Hive Mind launches keeps its *_DIR variable` in `rust/tests/web/issue-1161-host-contract.test.mjs`. |

It writes the config with `formal-ai with --globally` into a scratch home, copies the written directory to a temporary one, and starts the real CLI directly. The run uses an empty `HOME` and only one declared variable, which points at the copied directory (`*_DIR`/`*_HOME`) or file (the others). The case asserts that the session reaches `formal-ai serve` through the recording proxy and that nothing is written back into `HOME`. For `agent` this runs `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`. Pinned by `the_matrix_leg_serves_a_session_from_each_declared_relocation_variable`. Its first matrix run (37594789426) passed for `codex` (`CODEX_HOME`). For `agent` it showed that the relocated config is loaded and its `formalai` provider found, but the CLI's own default model outranks the config's `model`. The case therefore passes the model the way `formal-ai with` does, reading the new `model_arg`, `model_selector` and `model_arg_after_first_arg` fields of `formal-ai clients --format json`. With that, agentic CLI matrix run 37638262565 (head bb8759cdb, job "E2E (agent)" 112855726572) passed both agent relocations: `ok relocated: agent served a session from LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG=…/opencode.json` and `… from LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR=…`. Pinned by `the_matrix_leg_serves_a_session_from_each_declared_relocation_variable` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_env.rs`. |

## Issue #1163 Internet as Formal Knowledge

Issue [#1163](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1163) (E128,
part of the #1183 umbrella) turns fetched web pages into formal knowledge: one
generic page formalizer maps any fetched resource to a `LinkNetwork` (headings,
paragraphs, lists, tables, and language-tagged code blocks), search becomes the
entry point for a need no registered source covers, pages carry a data-driven
trust score and a rediscovery record, and queries over formalized pages answer
with links. The issue numbers its requirements 1 to 10; they are
`R1163-1` to `R1163-10` here in the same order. `R1163-11` to `R1163-16` are
the further obligations its "What to build", "How to test", "Design" and
"Definition of done" sections state without a number. The timeline, root
causes and prior art live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1163/`.

The module is `rust/src/web_formalize.rs` (with `rust/src/web_formalize_trust.rs`
included from it), not the `rust/src/page_formalizer.rs` the issue names; the
four test modules the issue sketches are consolidated in
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The browser twin is
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_web_formalize.js`, tested by
`rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1163-1 | A single `formalize_page(bytes, mime_hint) -> LinkNetwork` produces a `LinkNetwork` from any HTML, Markdown, plain-text, JSON, or PDF-text payload. | Implemented: `web_formalize::formalize_page` resolves the mime kind from the hint or the seed's sniff rules (`data/seed/page-formalization-rules.lino`) and builds a `page` root with one `heading` / `paragraph` / `list_item` / `table_row` / `code_block` child per block. Pinned by `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code`, `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback`, `generic_formalizer_covers_bespoke_statements` (JSON) and `plain_and_pdf_text_formalize` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The HTML walker once stepped over the whole document (an `<html>` open tag jumped the cursor past `</html>`) and the rule loaders once read no records (they iterated the top level, which holds only the file wrapper); both are fixed on this branch and the HTML test fails if either returns. Note: the network is assembled by inserting links, not by `LinkNetwork::parse`, and bare source files take the plain-text path. |
| R1163-2 | Every code block carries a language tag from the fence annotation, the HTML class, or a heuristic; an unrecognized fence yields `unknown`, never an empty tag. | Implemented: `resolve_language` walks the seed's `tag_source` order (fence, `html_class` with the seed's `language-` and `highlight ` class prefixes, the latter reading GitHub-style `highlight-source-<x>`, shebang and URL-extension heuristic) and falls back to the seed's `unknown`. Pinned by `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback` (fences `rust` and `shell`, bare fence `unknown`), `scala_page_tags_language_through_class_prefix`, `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code` and `heuristic_tier_tags_unannotated_fences` (shebang `python`, URL extension `rust`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`, and in the browser twin by the fence, class and heuristic tests of `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. Gap: an annotated fence the seed does not know (for example a made-up tag) passes through verbatim rather than becoming `unknown`, and the URL-extension tier matches a suffix anywhere in the URL (`.c` would match `.com`), so it relies on the seed's row order. |
| R1163-3 | For each of the six bespoke extractors, `formalize_page` on the same fixture bytes yields every statement the bespoke extractor yields (generic ⊇ bespoke). | Implemented on fixtures: `concept_lookup::extractor_statements` exposes what each of the six bespoke extractors yields (the four lexical readers through `read_glosses`, `oeis_sequence_v1` through the new `oeis::record_statements`, `python_docs_v1` through `python_docs::page_statements`, which now shares `page_definitions` with the index builder), and `generic_formalizer_covers_every_bespoke_extractor` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs` pins each extractor's real output exactly on its own fixture under `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1163/<extractor>/` and checks the generic network covers it; `wiktionary_entry_v1` keeps its earlier test. The HTML walker gained `<dt>` as a list item so a reference page's signature line is a statement (mirrored in the browser twin). The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: the five new fixtures are hand-trimmed payloads in each API's shape, not byte captures, and the bespoke Python reader inserts a space at every inline tag where the generic walker does not, so pages with inline markup inside a signature compare only modulo whitespace. |

## Issue #1164 Code Node Decomposition

Issue [#1164](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1164) (E129,
part of the #1183 umbrella) makes retrieved code examples formal knowledge: an
example is parsed into the meta language, decomposed into meaningful parts
(entry point, output operation, string literal, import, build and run
commands), generalized across languages by aligning those parts, and
recomposed for a new requirement. The issue states `R1164-1` to `R1164-11`;
`R1164-12` to `R1164-15` are the further obligations of its "Tests" and
"Definition of done" sections. The timeline, root causes and prior art live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1164/`.

The module is `rust/src/code_example_knowledge.rs`, not the
`rust/src/coding/code_node_decomposer.rs` the issue names; the two test
modules the issue sketches are consolidated in
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs`. The part vocabulary
is data in `data/seed/code-example-parts.lino`, which stores no program text:
recomposition builds from the decomposed examples. The browser twin is
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_examples.js`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1164-1 | `decompose_code_node` returns `DecomposeError::UnknownGrammar(<slug>)` for a slug with no entry in `data/seed/program-cst-grammars.lino`; it never guesses. | Implemented: the grammar lookup through `coding::cst::grammar_metadata` runs before anything else. Pinned by `unknown_grammar_slug_returns_unknown_grammar_error` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs` (`zig` and `pascal` both refused by name). |
| R1164-2 | For every registered slug, `decompose_code_node` parses through `LinkNetwork::parse` and returns at least one output operation, string literal, and entry point where the language has one. | Implemented: the parse goes through `LinkNetwork::parse` with the seed's grammar label; `decompose_rust_hello_world_produces_entry_output_literal`, `decompose_go_hello_world_produces_entry_output_literal`, `decompose_python_script_has_no_entry_point`, `every_captured_fixture_decomposes` and `registered_languages_decompose_output_and_literal` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs` check the output operation and literal for all fifteen registered slugs (rust, go, python, kotlin, swift, scala, javascript, typescript, java, csharp, c, cpp, ruby, php, r), and `r` now has a `part_language` row in the seed. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. Gap: the entry point is asserted only for rust, go and kotlin. |

Exercised by every decomposition test in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs`. Gap: no ratchet fails the build if a language literal is later added to the module. |

## Issue #1165 Discovery on the Production Path

Issue [#1165](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1165) (E130)
puts the coding-by-discovery machinery on the path users and Hive Mind hit:
every stored program becomes a *cache entry* that names where a rediscovery
starts from, a cache miss routes to `research_coding_skill_gap` instead of a
template literal, and the whole cache is deletable by design. The analysis
and the wiring plan live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1165/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1165-1 | When the solver selects `SelectedRule::WriteProgram` and no cached procedure exists for the language/task, `research_coding_skill_gap` runs on the miss path and the answer is discovery-backed. | Partial (2026-10-07, this pull request): the `WriteProgram` branch of `rust/src/solver.rs` loads the procedure cache and calls `discovery_production::cached_write_program`; a verified row for the `(language, task)` pair replaces the catalog template in both the answer and the `ExecutionRecipe`, with a `procedure_cache` hit event in the derivation, and a prompt that customised the template keeps its own program. Pinned by `write_program_reuses_the_cached_procedure_only_for_an_unmodified_request` (Rust and JS). The miss path now names its gap instead of hiding it: the policy seed `data/seed/program-cache-policy.lino` gains a `miss_route` record (research requires `expected_output` and `reviewer_approval`; a solve carries `expected_output`), `discovery_production::miss_research_missing` (JS twin `missResearchMissing`) reads it, and an unmodified request with no cache row logs `procedure_cache outcome=miss language=... task=... research_missing=reviewer_approval`. Pinned by `miss_route_names_what_research_lacks_on_a_solve` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1165_discovery_production.rs` (drafted without a local cargo run) and its JS twin. Open: research itself does not run on a solve, because no solve call carries a reviewer's `CodingResearchApproval`; the answer on a miss is still the template. Third pass (2026-10-07): the discovery a miss would run now exists outside this module: the #1164 decomposer recomposes a Hello World program from the real captures under `rust/tests/fixtures/coding-discovery/captured/` (Rust Book, go.dev, kotlinlang, Scala book, Swift book). Running it over those captures in the browser engine (the case-study procedure) shows why it is not yet wired in as the answer: the page formalizer strips each code line's leading whitespace in both roots (`strip_tags_keep_lines`, `rust/src/web_formalize.rs`, and `pageStripTagsKeepLines`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_web_formalize.js`, both apply the per-line tag stripper to `<pre>` text), so every recomposed program comes back unindented (`fn main() {\nprintln!(...);\n}`). Answering from it would regress the programs users get, and the fix belongs to the formalizer (#1163). Separately, the captures are test fixtures, not shipped source data, so an offline production solve has nothing to rediscover from. Fourth pass (2026-10-08): the miss is now discovery-backed for every pair with documentation captures. The formalizer blocker is fixed in both roots (`strip_tags_keep_lines` / `pageStripTagsKeepLines` keep each line's indentation and drop only the blank lines around a block and the indentation all its lines share; pinned by `a_code_block_keeps_its_indentation` and its JS twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-1164-captured-pages.test.mjs`). The captures ship as pre-cached source data: `data/seed/coding-documentation-captures.lino` holds, per captured page (Rust Book, go.dev, kotlinlang command-line and tour, Scala book), its URL, rediscovery query, fixture path and SHA-256 and the code blocks the formalizer reads from those bytes, written by `scripts/generate-coding-documentation-captures.mjs` and re-derived from the fixtures by `documentation_captures_are_the_formalized_fixtures` (Rust) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1165-documentation-captures.test.mjs`; the policy seed's new `documentation_route` record declares the route and its two verifications. On an unmodified miss the `WriteProgram` branch calls `discovery_production::answer_cache_miss` (`rust/src/discovery_production_documentation.rs`; JS twin `rediscoverDocumentedProgram` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_examples.js`): each page's first block that decomposes into an output call printing a literal is recomposed by the #1164 decomposer with the task's expected output bound into the literal, the shortest program is kept, and it is answered only when decomposing it again finds the same call printing the expected output and it declares every name the catalog run contract invokes. The derivation logs `procedure_cache outcome=discovered language=... task=... rediscovery_source=<page> content_id=0x...`; the row is stored in a configured runtime cache (`FORMAL_AI_PROCEDURE_CACHE`, never the committed file) and the next request is a hit. Rust, Go and Kotlin Hello World are answered this way; the Scala book's `object hello` is refused (`documentation_rejected=run_contract:Main`, since the catalog runs `scala Main`) and keeps the stored template. Pinned by `documentation_rediscovery_recomposes_the_captured_example_and_checks_the_run_contract`, `write_program_miss_answers_from_the_documentation`, `a_rejected_documented_example_is_named_on_the_miss` and `a_rediscovered_row_is_stored_and_reused` (Rust, drafted without a local cargo run), and by the R1165-1 cases of `issue-1165-worker-procedure-cache.test.mjs` and `issue-1165-server-procedure-cache.test.mjs` (record in the runtime cache, reuse as a hit, committed cache untouched). Still open: `research_coding_skill_gap` itself does not run on a solve (no reviewer approval), and a pair without a captured page (Python, C, Java, ...) is still the template with the research miss named; capturing a documentation page per catalog language is the remaining work. Fifth pass (2026-10-08): every catalog language with an official page whose example the catalog can run is now rediscovered. Eight more pages are captured byte for byte under `rust/tests/fixtures/coding-discovery/captured/` and SHA-pinned in the captures seed: the Python wiki's simple examples (`print('Hello, world!')`), MDN's console page (`console.log("Hello, world!");`), the TypeScript handbook basics (`hello.ts` with its comment line), Microsoft's C `puts` page, C++ console page and C# Hello World tutorial, ruby-lang.org's Hello World example (with its comment header) and the Swift book's guided tour. A captured block tagged with a surface of its `program_language` meaning (`js`, `ts`, `c++`) names that language (`block_names_language` / `documentationBlockNamesLanguage`). Every rediscovered program was saved under its run contract and run locally (node, tsc, gcc, g++, dotnet, ruby, swift, python3), printing exactly `Hello, world!` and a newline. Pinned by the R1165-1 cases of `rust/tests/web/issue-1165-worker-procedure-cache.test.mjs` (ten languages, exact program and `content_id`), `rust/tests/web/issue-1165-documentation-captures.test.mjs` and `retired_seed_programs_are_reproduced_by_the_documentation` (Rust, solver `execution_recipe.source` per language, drafted without a local cargo run). Still open, with the reason: Java (no official page declares a class `Main`; dev.java, the Oracle tutorial and the JEPs use `HelloWorldApp`, `MyFirstClass` or `HelloWorld`, so the run contract `java Main` refuses them), Scala (the only official example declaring `Main` is a scala-cli page whose block carries a `//> using dep` directive for an unused library; the Scala book stays captured and refused as `run_contract:Main`), PHP (php.net's first example ends in `?>` with no newline, so it prints `Hello, world!` without the trailing newline the catalog verified), R (no official page has a lone `print` or `cat` example; the manuals' first output blocks bind the literal into a wrong program), Laravel (no grammar row, and the Artisan docs show no Hello World command). `research_coding_skill_gap` itself still does not run on a solve (no reviewer approval). Sixth pass (2026-10-08): Java, Scala and PHP are rediscovered too, so every catalog language but R and Laravel answers from documentation. The run contract now binds a documented program's own name the way kotlinlang's `hello.kt` binds `Main.kt` (`documented_run_contract` in `rust/src/discovery_production_contract.rs`, JS `documentedRunContract`): Oracle's Java tutorial for Unix (captured) declares `class HelloWorldApp` and states `javac HelloWorldApp.java` and `java HelloWorldApp`, so the answer saves `HelloWorldApp.java` and runs the page's commands; the Scala book's `object hello` binds through the part vocabulary's new `entry_container` row (`hello.scala`, `scalac hello.scala`, `scala hello`). php.net's first example (`echo "Hello, world!";` then `?>`) prints no trailing newline; rather than normalise the output check (the catalog verifies exact output), the derivation records the deviation (`documentation_deviation language=php task=hello_world trailing_newline=absent`, from the new `bare_output_call` and `newline_token` rows). The Java program was compiled and run locally (`Hello, world!` and a newline). Pinned by `a_documented_program_binds_its_run_contract_and_records_each_command_source`, `the_documented_run_contract_of_every_bound_language`, `only_the_php_page_example_prints_no_trailing_newline` (Rust, drafted without a local cargo run) and the R1165-6 cases of `rust/tests/web/issue-1165-worker-procedure-cache.test.mjs` and `issue-1165-documentation-captures.test.mjs`. Still open: R (no official page has a standalone `print`/`cat` example) and Laravel (no grammar row; the Artisan docs show no Hello World command). Seventh pass (2026-10-08): an answer no longer borrows a run that did not verify its program. The policy seed's new `recorded_verification` names, by `content_id`, the Hello World programs the issue-8 harness ran; a documentation-sourced program cites that run only when its id is recorded (Rust, Go and JavaScript are byte-identical to what ran), and every other one says "not run; this program was rediscovered from <page> and its output contract was checked by decomposition, not by executing it" (seed response `program_execution_rediscovered` in en, ru, hi, zh and es; `data/meta/server-messages.lino` for the JS server), with the unverified output label and no borrowed notes. The derivation logs `program_verification` (content id, `recorded` or `decomposition`, the environment or the page) and the native `execution_status`/`execution_environment` events follow. Pinned by `a_documented_program_cites_only_the_run_that_verified_it`, the updated exact answers (`prompt_variations.rs`, `selection.rs`, `formal_ai.rs`, `issue_412_oracle_languages.rs`, `issue_1021_behaviour_range.rs`) and the JS cases in `issue-1165-worker-procedure-cache.test.mjs` and `server-evidence-links.test.mjs`. Lua is now rediscovered from lua.org's Programming in Lua (meta-language ships tree-sitter-lua; its grammar row is registered by hand like Pascal's). Still open, with reasons: R (no official page's first printing block is a standalone example: stat.ethz.ch's cat page yields its Usage line, print.default's a format call, R-intro's an account closure), Laravel (the routing page's `Route::get('/', fn () => 'Hello World')` returns an HTTP response body, not the standard output the catalog's `php artisan hello:world` contract checks, and the decomposer finds no output call in it), Bash and Haskell (meta-language ships no grammar for either, so no page can be decomposed; an upstream grammar is the prerequisite). Eighth pass (2026-10-08, DISCOVER): re-checked, unchanged for programs. meta-language 0.58.2 is still the newest release on crates.io and ships no Bash or Haskell grammar, so no page can be decomposed for either; writing cache rows for Bash, Haskell or Laravel by hand would be memorization with a verified label (and would raise the R1165-8 ratchet), so none were written. The check and run commands are now discovery-backed wherever a captured page states them (R1165-6). |

## Issue #1166 The Request Formalized into Obligations

Issue [#1166](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1166) (E131)
replaces phrase matching with request formalization: an issue body parses
into an obligation graph whose nodes carry semantic kinds and anchored
literals, mentions of the same quoted literal collapse to one node (the
structural fix for the Kotlin doubled output of #1156), and nothing
underivable is silently discarded. The root-cause analysis lives in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1166/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1166-1 | An issue body parses into an `ObligationGraph`; every enumerated requirement produces an `ObligationNode` anchored to seed meanings/roles. | Implemented: `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs` (`formalize_request`) builds on `obligation_ledger::ObligationNode::build` — no new ledger type — and classifies clauses against `print_stdout`, `ci_workflow_request`, and the program-request roles. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. |
| R1166-2 | Two or more mentions of the same quoted literal produce exactly one output-literal node. | Implemented: `coreference_pass` merges by literal value across clauses; `two_identical_output_clauses_produce_one_node` proves three mentions (intro, "print exactly", Expected Output) yield one node and one value. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `coreferencePass` and the new `uniqueOutputLiteral`/`literalFor` in `js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs` hold the same cases. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-3 | The executor derives its plan from obligation nodes and reports undischargeable nodes with byte spans. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; the JS root verified locally, the Rust root awaiting CI). The graph exposes `obligations_of_kind` and `gap_report` (node id + byte span + reason). The executor's CI-workflow decision comes from the graph: `ci_workflow::requested_in` delegates to `intent_formalization::request_demands(objective, ObligationKind::CiWorkflow)`, and its JS twin `requestedIn` (`js/agentic/ci_workflow.mjs`) reads the same clause nodes (`ci_workflow_demand_is_read_from_the_obligation_graph`, Rust and JS). The program executor's output operands come from the graph too: `program_contract::explicit_stdout` and its JS twin `explicitStdout` read `intent_formalization::bound_output_literals` (`js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs` `boundOutputLiterals`), which assigns every quoted segment to the enumerated obligation clause (`clauses_with_spans`) that contains it and binds it when its introduction inside that clause evidences the seed `print_stdout` meaning, each value once. The routing change this makes, pinned in both roots: a print verb in an earlier enumerated clause no longer binds a literal in a later one (`Print the greeting! Then "Hello"` binds nothing; the old reading bound `Hello` because `!` was not one of its breaks); every other shape binds as before. The graph's broader `OutputLiteral` classification is kept for reporting rather than binding, so it cannot widen which prompts get a program contract; a literal it demands that the binding does not carry is reported (R1166-4). The clause vocabularies (output verbs, code style, file naming, CI badge) moved out of code into the seed roles `output_obligation_verb`, `code_style_obligation`, `file_naming_obligation` and `ci_badge_obligation` (`data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino`), which the JS port reads too. The JS ledger's `opensAClause` now reads a line break before trimming, as the Rust `opens_a_clause` has since #1166, so both roots enumerate the same clauses. Pinned by the shared fixture `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/executor-gaps.json` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-executor-gaps.test.mjs`) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. The parity corpus `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` has no program-contract case and the browser runtime is the Rust worker, so the Rust/JS twin parity for this routing lives in that shared fixture instead. |
| R1166-4 | A completed run emits an obligation report for each undischargeable node; none is silently omitted. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; the JS root verified locally, the Rust root awaiting CI). `intent_formalization::obligation_gap_lines` is the report: the `gap_report` lines (clauses no rule can read) followed by `ObligationGraph::unbound_output_report` (output literals the graph demands that the executor's binding does not carry, under the `output_literal_not_bound_by_executor` reason of the `unbound_output_literal` rule in `data/meta/obligation-evidence-contract.lino`), so a demanded value the program would not print is no longer omitted silently. `record_obligation_gaps` writes each line as an `obligation_gap` event from every executor that reads the graph: the program-contract executor (`coding::program_contract::answer`, used by the solver and the agentic planner) and the catalog `write_program` executor in `rust/src/solver.rs` whenever the request formalizes into work obligations or demands the CI workflow the agentic work-item executor attaches. The JS agentic root keeps no event log, so its executor `programContractAnswer` (used by `js/agentic/planner.mjs` and `js/agentic/general_execution.mjs`) carries the same lines as `obligation_gaps`; the catalog `write_program` arm is native-only there (documented in `general_execution.mjs`), so that emission has no JS twin. The browser worker (`js/worker/`) records the same events (2026-10-07, verified locally): its catalog `WriteProgram` tail (`solverWriteProgramEvents`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_solver_events.js`) appends `solverObligationGapEvents` between `legacy_intent` and `procedure_cache`, where the native branch records them, behind the same gate. The port is `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligations.js` (clause enumeration, the clause-level ledger tree with its one-level checkable split, `derive_expectation`, the seed-role classifier, coreference, `bound_output_literals`, `obligation_gap_lines`) and `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligation_plans.js` (the general-planner mode `derive_expectation` consults, never the plan itself). Its vocabulary is the seed lexicon; the two `data/meta` decisions the worker cannot fetch (the expectation rules of `obligation-evidence-contract.lino` and the approved `missing_operation_contract` strategy of `task-decomposition-strategies.lino`) are mirrored in the worker and held equal to the files by its test. The fixture's `catalogCases` pin six catalog requests, five carrying work or CI obligations (one with an unbound output literal) and one carrying none, in the worker (`rust/tests/web/issue-1166-worker-obligation-gaps.test.mjs`: exact events, order and position; it also holds the worker's lines, plan modes and checkable splits equal to the agentic root on every fixture prompt and fourteen plan-shaped prompts) and in the native solver (`catalog_requests_record_the_worker_gap_lines` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, awaiting CI; it checks the exact lines and their presence in the run's Links Notation, not their order there). Still open: the worker port is a hand mirror, not the Rust-to-WASM path the worker line budget asks for, so it must be kept in step with the Rust module by these tests. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_executor_gaps.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-executor-gaps.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-worker-obligation-gaps.test.mjs`, which assert the same fixture lines (node ids, spans, reasons) in the native, agentic and worker roots. |
| R1166-5 | An underivable clause yields `ObligationExpectation::Underivable`, split or reported, never discarded. | Implemented and pinned: `unknown_requirement_clause_yields_underivable_node_not_panic` (the ledger's own expectation semantics; the classifier leaves such nodes unclassified). JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `underivable` and `gapReport` keep the clause with its span. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-6 | A translated body (en/ru/hi/zh/es) yields the same graph modulo the language tag. | Implemented for the fixture family: `kotlin_issue_ru_yields_same_obligation_count_as_en` and `kotlin_issue_hi_zh_es_yield_same_graph_modulo_language_tag` over `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/hello-world-kotlin-{en,ru,hi,zh,es}.txt`; classification reads the seed lexicon's multilingual lexemes only; since 2026-10-07 the style, naming, badge and output-verb vocabularies are seed roles (`data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino`) rather than code-side tables. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): `obligationKinds` (declaration order, as the Rust `Ord`) over the same five fixtures. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-7 | A paraphrased body produces an equivalent graph. | Implemented: `paraphrase_en_yields_same_obligation_count_as_canonical_en` over `hello-world-kotlin-paraphrase-en.txt`. JavaScript root (2026-10-07): the same paraphrase fixture. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |
| R1166-8 | Routing decides by the formalized request, not the leading word. | Implemented for the terminal router: `leading_shell_command` in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` now consults `request_carries_work_obligations` — a quoted output literal plus an authoring clause (program, CI, style, naming, badge) is a sentence about building something, in any of the five languages, while `git status` and `echo "Hello, World!"` stay commands (`work_obligation_requests_are_not_terminal_commands`). JavaScript roots (2026-10-07): `requestCarriesWorkObligations` in the agentic port, and the browser worker's terminal router: `leadingShellCommand` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js`) now returns no command when `obligationCarriesWork` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_obligations.js`, the gate the catalog arm already used, split out) finds work obligations — before this the worker treated `make kotlin app printing "Hello, World!" plus GitHub Actions workflow`, whose words all parse as arguments, as a `make` command line. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1166-obligation-routing.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1168 Generated Code Uses Versions Resolved at Generation Time

Issue [#1168](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1168) (E133)
makes every third-party version a generated artifact pins — action refs,
toolchain versions, the Java LTS — a *resolved* value with provenance, never a
memorized string. Resolution happens at generation time from the publisher's
own API, is recorded in the derivation, and degrades loudly (cache, then
shipped baseline, each said out loud) rather than silently going stale.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1168-1 | The latest release tag and its commit SHA for every third-party GitHub Action in a generated CI workflow are fetched from `https://api.github.com/repos/{publisher}/{repo}/releases/latest` (then `commits/{tag}` for the SHA). | Implemented: `resolve_github` in `rust/src/version_resolution.rs`, covering `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-java`, `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`, `actions/setup-python`; pinned by mocked-transport tests (`resolves_every_pin_from_live_fixtures`). Generation-time path (2026-10-07): `VersionSet::for_generation` now opens its `CachedSourceClient` online when `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH` is set (the repository's live-retrieval opt-in); before, it was always offline, so a generated workflow never read a publisher's API. The JavaScript root has the same ladder: `js/agentic/crate/source_cache.mjs` mirrors `CachedSourceClient::fetch` over an injected io in the native cache layout, and `forGeneration()` reads the installed host's `sourceFetch` (`js/agentic/node-host.mjs`: `FORMAL_AI_SOURCE_CACHE_DIR`, curl under `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-source-cache.test.mjs`. |
| R1168-2 | The Kotlin version is the latest `JetBrains/kotlin` release tag. | Implemented in the same module (`v2.4.20` as shipped baseline); the tag feeds `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`'s `version:` argument through `fill_workflow_versions`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` (`resolves_every_pin_from_live_fixtures`) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-source-cache.test.mjs`. |
| R1168-3 | The Java version is Adoptium's own `most_recent_lts`, never a literal `'21'`. | Implemented: `resolve_java_lts` reads `https://api.adoptium.net/v3/info/available_releases` (25 as shipped baseline). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` (`resolves_every_pin_from_live_fixtures`, `java_lts` tag 25 with no SHA) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-source-cache.test.mjs`. |
| R1168-4 | Every resolved version is recorded in the derivation as a `SourceCapture` (source_url, fetched_at, sha256, cached, bytes) via the existing `CachedSourceClient`. | Implemented: `VersionSet::record` appends each capture's provenance plus one `version_resolution` line per pin; pinned by `records_the_resolution_in_the_derivation`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` and, for the JavaScript root, `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-source-cache.test.mjs`. |
| R1168-5 | When the live API is unreachable, the most recent cached capture is used and the answer is annotated `(version resolved from cache; fetched_at=<timestamp>)`. | Implemented: `CachedSourceClient` replay supplies `Origin::Cache`, and `provenance_note` emits exactly that wording — extended to the shipped baseline, which annotates `(version resolved from the shipped baseline measured <date>)`; `ci_workflow::render` prepends the notes as workflow comments. Pinned by `offline_replays_the_cached_capture_and_says_so`. The JavaScript source cache applies the same 60-day TTL and offline replay. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs` (`offline_replays_the_cached_capture_and_says_so`, `empty_cache_falls_back_to_the_shipped_baseline`) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-source-cache.test.mjs`. |
| R1168-6 | `workflow_template` and `ci_setup` values carry placeholders, never literal SHAs or bare versions. | Implemented (2026-10-07, this pull request). `fill_workflow_versions` fills `{checkout_ref}` … `{java_lts}` plus the new `{setup_coursier_ref}`/`{setup_coursier_tag}`/`{scala_version}`, and still rewrites any stale `@<sha>` / `version: '…'` literal that slips through, scoped per action block. The last literal template row is gone: the Scala `ci_setup` in `data/meta/stdout-program-contracts.lino` (and its embedded mirror) now reads `coursier/setup-action@{setup_coursier_ref} # {setup_coursier_tag}`, `jvm: temurin:{java_lts}` and `apps: scala:{scala_version} scalac:{scala_version}`. `VersionSet` resolves `coursier/setup-action` and `scala/scala` (shipped baselines v3.0.4 @ 648df969… and 2.13.18, measured 2026-10-07 from the GitHub releases API, in `data/seed/toolchains.lino`). `work-item-steps.lino` already carried placeholders only. Pinned by `fills_the_scala_ci_setup_placeholders` and `repository_data_carries_no_memorized_pin` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs`. |
| R1168-7 | A CI gate fails on any `@<sha>` or bare version literal for a third-party action or toolchain in `data/`. | Implemented: `scripts/check-generated-version-literals.rs` (scans `data/` minus `data/cache/`; the toolchains baseline is exempt by shape, not by name), with embedded tests plus `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs`, where `repository_data_carries_no_memorized_pin` now asserts zero findings in the repository's `data/`. The gate is registered as a CI stage in `data/meta/ci-gates/check-generated-version-literals.lino` (stage `rust`). |
| R1168-8 | Three-roots parity: `version_resolution.rs` translated to js/ts and parity cases added. | Implemented (2026-10-07, this pull request; JavaScript verified locally, Rust awaiting CI). JS root: `js/agentic/crate/version_resolution.mjs` mirrors `VersionSet::resolve` (`resolveVersionSet`, over an injected `fetch` that stands in for `CachedSourceClient`, with the same live → cache → baseline ladder and capture order), `VersionSet::record` (`recordVersionSet`), the coursier/Scala pins, and `VersionSet::for_generation` (`forGeneration(fetch)`, the shipped baseline when the host passes no fetch); `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-version-resolution-parity.test.mjs` reproduces the Rust unit cases (6 tests). TS root: `ts/agentic/crate/version_resolution.mts` and `ts/agentic/ci_workflow.mts` are generated by `scripts/translate-es.mjs`. Parity over the generated pins: the agentic planner's workflow render now takes its version source by injection in both runtimes -- Rust `ci_workflow::render_with(recipe, versions)` (re-exported as `formal_ai::agentic_coding::render_ci_workflow`) and JS `renderWith(recipe, versions)` in `js/agentic/ci_workflow.mjs`; `render` injects the generation-time set. Correction to the earlier re-check: `VersionSet::for_generation` never reaches the network -- `CachedSourceClient::new` builds the client with `online: false`, so the native ladder is cache → baseline, and with no source cache it is the baseline, as `forGeneration()` is in JS. `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1168/workflow-render-parity.json` pins the full workflow text the planner attaches for the Kotlin, Python, Scala and Rust program-contract prompts, rendered from the offline shipped baseline; `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_workflow_render_parity.rs` (via `program_contract::answer` and `render_ci_workflow`) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-workflow-render-parity.test.mjs` (via `programContractAnswer` and `renderWith`, 2 tests passing locally) assert the same text. Not a `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` case: that fixture drives `UniversalSolver::solve` and the browser worker's `solve`, and neither answers with a workflow (`program_contract::answer` returns the program and its recipe; the workflow is attached by the agentic planner), so the planner lane is where the pins are compared. Since 2026-10-07 the Node host owns the source cache too (`js/agentic/crate/source_cache.mjs`, R1168-1), so JavaScript generation replays the same `FORMAL_AI_SOURCE_CACHE_DIR` captures the native host does; only the browser host, which reads no files, answers from the baseline. |

## Issue #1169 Every Dependency at Its Latest Release

Issue [#1169](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1169) (E134)
makes dependency currency a fact the repository enforces, not a habit it
hopes for: every dependency — crates, npm packages, GitHub Action refs, the
container base image, the rustc floor — sits at its publisher's latest
release, and a gate fails when one does not. The one sanctioned hold-back is
an in-tree annotation naming the issue that tracks it.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1169-1 | A gate reads every ecosystem the repository declares: `rust/Cargo.toml` against `rust/Cargo.lock`, every `package.json` against its lockfile (manifest-range fallback where a directory ships no lock), `uses:` refs in `.github/workflows` and composite actions, `FROM` bases in the `Dockerfile`, and the `rust-version` floor. | Implemented: `collect` in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest.rs`, walking with `node_modules`/`target`/`.git`/`.claude`/`cache` excluded; pinned by `the_repository_tree_collects_every_ecosystem` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs`. |
| R1169-2 | "Latest" comes from the publisher's own registry — crates.io `max_stable_version`, npm `dist-tags.latest`, GitHub `releases/latest`, Docker Hub tags, the rust stable channel — never a memorized list. | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07): the `latest_*` fetchers (curl + `USER_AGENT`, 30 s cap) hand each body to a pure reader in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest-parsers.rs` — `crates_io_latest` (`max_stable_version`), `npm_latest` (`dist-tags.latest`), `github_latest` (`tag_name`), `docker_hub_latest` (the highest dotted-numeric tag, so `latest`, suffixed variants and a rebuilt old tag listed first do not win) and `rust_channel_latest` (`[pkg.rust]` `version`, first word). This pass fixed three readers that could not have answered: the JSON reader required `"key":"value"` with no space, which api.github.com never sends (it pretty-prints `"tag_name": "v7.0.1"`); the rust channel reader looked for a `[rust]` section the channel file does not have; and a sub-path action (`github/codeql-action/init`) was asked for releases of a repository that does not exist (`action_repository` now asks `github/codeql-action`). The readers were also compiled out of every test build; they are now pure functions pinned against real-shaped answers by `registry_answers_parse_in_their_publishers_shapes` in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest-tests.rs`, which `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs` compiles into the unit suite. No live registry run was recorded locally. |
| R1169-3 | A dependency may be held back only with a same-line annotation naming the tracking issue; the gate verifies the annotation, and drift without one fails. | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07): `blocked_annotation` (Cargo.toml, same line) and the `"<name>//"` note of a package.json both go through `tracking_reference`, which accepts the first token of the reason, bare or `<…>`-bracketed, only when it is an `https://` issue URL (`…/issues/<n>`) or a published security advisory (`…/advisories/GHSA-…`, the record that tracks an unpatched vulnerability). Before this pass a package.json note was accepted with any text after `blocked:` and the documented `<https://…>` bracket form was rejected in Cargo.toml. Blocked findings print `(blocked)` and `exit_code` returns 0 for them, unblocked drift returns 1. `links-notation = "0.16.1" # blocked: …` was the first resident and was lifted on 2026-10-07 when codec 0.8.0 moved to links-notation 0.23 (the repository-tree test that still asserted it now asserts the current residents); the residents are the desktop `command-stream` note (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) and the desktop/VS Code `browser-commander` and `@kreuzberg/html-to-markdown-node` override notes. Documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Pinned by `blocked_notes_must_carry_a_tracking_reference` and `exit_codes_separate_drift_from_an_unverifiable_run` (embedded suite) and `the_repository_tree_collects_every_ecosystem` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs`. |
| R1169-4 | The tree itself is moved to latest: `cargo update` resolution (already applied to `rust/Cargo.lock` — command-stream 1.2.0, webrtc 0.21.0, toml_edit 0.25.15, clap 4.6.7 …), npm manifests hand-bumped with real registry integrity (react/react-dom 19.3.0, dompurify 3.4.16, marked 18.0.14, command-stream 1.2.0, electron 44.4.5, electron-builder 26.17.0 with its app-builder-lib/dmg-builder/builder-util/electron-publish/squirrel-windows ring, playwright 1.63.0 across desktop + e2e + vscode), and the pin edits (`konrad/box-dind` 2.10.2, `actions/cache` v6 in both composite actions, `zizmor-action` v0.6.4). | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07, this pull request). The listed moves are in the tree: `rust/Cargo.lock` resolves command-stream 1.2.0, webrtc 0.21.0, toml_edit 0.25.15 and clap 4.6.7; `package.json` pins react/react-dom 19.3.0, dompurify 3.4.16 and marked 18.0.14; `desktop/package.json` pins command-stream 1.2.0, electron ^44.4.5, electron-builder ^26.17.0 and playwright ^1.63.0; vscode and `rust/tests/e2e` pin playwright ^1.63.0 with their locks; `Dockerfile` runs `FROM konard/box-dind:2.10.2`; all three composite actions use `actions/cache@v6`; `zizmor-action@v0.6.4`. The desktop/e2e lock edits were verified closed by a before/after range-resolution diff over the `packages` map. The stale `konard/box-dind:2.1.1` comments in `Dockerfile.slim` and `container-images.yml` now name 2.10.2. The desktop and VS Code sandbox image now name `konard/box-dind:2.10.2` too (verified on Docker Hub as the current tag, published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64): `desktop/lib/tool-router.cjs` `SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `desktop/scripts/smoke.mjs`, `vscode/src/lib/config.cjs` `DEFAULT_IMAGE`, the `vscode/package.json` setting default, the `docker_microservice` environment of `data/seed/environments.lino` (embedded mirror too), README, `vscode/README.md` and the architecture/desktop/vscode docs, with `docker_runtime.rs`, `docs_requirements.rs` and `formal_ai_cli.rs` pinning 2.10.2. The one remaining 2.1.1 pin is the historical issue #195 case-study research note, which records what was true then. No desktop or VS Code smoke run against the new image was recorded locally; the pinning tests run in CI. |
| R1169-5 | A daily job refreshes the registry answers, applies every unblocked bump, re-resolves lockfiles, re-runs the CI gates, and opens one PR with whatever moved. | Implemented (2026-10-07): `.github/workflows/dependencies-latest.yml` (cron `23 5 * * *`, off the fleet's :00 stampede per issue #1021, plus `workflow_dispatch`) installs what it runs — the release workflow's Rust toolchain, Bun from `.bun-version`, Node 22 and `rust-script` through `scripts/install-rust-script.sh` (the earlier draft never installed `rust-script` and could not have run) — then `--refresh-snapshot`, `--apply --offline` failing on any exit other than 0 or 1, `cargo update --workspace`, one lock-only re-resolution per committed lockfile by the tool that owns it (`bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock`, `npm install --package-lock-only` for `package-lock.json`; the draft ran `bun install --mode=save || true` in npm directories and swallowed every failure), the three `run-ci-gates` stages with the WASM worker and web bundle builds they need, and `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8`. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1169-dependencies-latest-workflow.test.mjs` (5 tests, passing locally). The first scheduled run happens on the default branch after merge; no run of it was recorded from this branch. |
| R1169-6 | Registry flakiness never reddens CI: `--offline` answers from `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`, written by `--refresh-snapshot`; an unreachable registry exits 3, distinct from findings. | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07): `read_snapshot`/`write_snapshot` (flat lino, one `registry_entry <ecosystem>/<name>` record per answer) and the exit-code ladder 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 usage / 3 unverifiable. `offline_snapshot` makes an absent snapshot an error naming `--refresh-snapshot`, and `main` exits `EXIT_UNVERIFIABLE` (3) on it, so a missing or unreachable registry answer never reads as "no findings" nor as drift. The repository commits no `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`: the first `--refresh-snapshot` run (the daily job of R1169-5) writes it from live answers, and none was fabricated here. Pinned by `offline_without_a_snapshot_is_unverifiable_not_clean` and `offline_gate_flags_drift_and_honors_blocked_annotations` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs`, plus `snapshot_round_trip` and `exit_codes_separate_drift_from_an_unverifiable_run` in the embedded suite. |
| R1169-7 | `--apply` moves manifests (not lockfiles) and leaves annotated pins alone; lockfiles are re-derived by the daily job's resolvers. | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07): `apply_latest` + the per-ecosystem line rewriters move manifests and `uses:`/`FROM`/`rust-version` lines, never lockfiles, and skip every finding that carries a blocked annotation. Workflow refs are compared and rewritten at their own precision: a moving branch or tool selector (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, `taiki-e/install-action@nextest`) is not a release pin and is not collected; a floating major (`@v7`) is current while the latest release is a `7.x.y` (`selects_latest`) and moves to `@v8`, not `@v8.0.1` (`same_precision`); `rewrite_uses_line` matches the declared ref with its `v`, which the earlier draft dropped, so a `@v6` line was never rewritten; a 40-hex commit SHA is reported unverifiable. Pinned by `apply_moves_unblocked_manifests_and_leaves_blocked_alone` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs` and `action_refs_float_and_rewrite_at_their_own_precision`, `apply_rewrites_manifests_not_locks` and `apply_leaves_blocked_lines_alone` in the embedded suite. |
| R1169-8 | The gate's parsers and rules are pinned by tests that compile the script into the unit suite. | Implemented: sixteen embedded tests in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest-tests.rs` (the script's `#[cfg(test)]` module; eleven before the 2026-10-07 pass) plus four fixture-tree tests in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs` (`#[path]` include, the `ci_gates.rs` idiom). |

The unit suite registers `issue_1169_dependency_currency` in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`. The first live `--refresh-snapshot` run (2026-10-07,
79 entries) is committed as `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`, so
the gate now runs on every pull request through
`data/meta/ci-gates/check-dependencies-latest.lino` (`--offline`, after the
embedded tests). That run exposed and fixed five collector bugs: multi-stage
aliases (`FROM builder`) and official images without `library/` looked up on
Docker Hub, anonymous GitHub API calls exhausting the hourly limit (a
`GH_TOKEN` now reaches api.github.com only, via curl's stdin config), string
rather than numeric drift (a pin past a lagging dist-tag read as drift), and a
`rust:1.98-slim` rewrite that dropped the `-slim` variant. Every manifest was
then moved to the snapshot's latest. Floating major `uses:` refs (`@v7`) are no
longer findings while their major is the latest, and moving refs (`@stable`)
are not collected, so the remaining first-run findings are real drift.
