## Issue #1172 Factual QA Subject-Verified Lookup

Issue [#1172](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1172) (E137,
part of the #1183 umbrella) reports that "What is the capital of Australia?"
was answered with "The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C." —
the alias "us" matched as a raw substring inside "a**us**tralia". A wrong
answer is worse than no answer. This shard pins the delivered word-boundary
fix (R1, R4, R10, R11 of the issue), the subject Q-id gate (R2), seeded
comparisons (R6), questions over prompt-supplied text (R7) and the shared
parity case (R1172-12), and records the open follow-ups (R3, R5, R8, R9 and
the live-data halves of R6/R7) honestly. The root-cause
analysis, the corrected issue-0127 rows, and
the evidence live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1172/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1172-1 | A subject alias or question keyword may match the normalized prompt only at word boundaries (tokenized comparison), never as a raw substring inside a longer word: "us" must not match inside "australia"; multi-word aliases ("united states") match as consecutive token sequences; CJK surfaces, which have no inter-word spaces, keep substring matching. | Implemented: `FactRecord::matches_normalized` (`rust/src/seed/facts.rs`) now gates every alias and keyword through the new associated `FactRecord::contains_word_sequence`, which tokenizes the phrase with the same `engine::normalize_prompt` the caller applied to the prompt and requires a consecutive token run — the same contract as `seed::meanings::surface_present` (issue #386), mirrored for the fact store's own matching path. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_subject_match.rs`. |
| R1172-2 | A fact record may answer only when the formalized question's subject (Wikidata Q-id) equals the record's `subject_qid`; alias/keyword matching is retired as the primary mechanism. | Implemented (JavaScript verified locally; the Rust twin is drafted and awaits CI, no local `cargo` run): the subject gate. The question's subject is formalized — the browser worker's `parseFactQuestion` slot, the native `formalize_prompt_candidates` subject anchor when it is already a Wikidata item, otherwise the clause of the prompt that carries the asked `fact_relation` — and resolved to one Q-id through the fact store's own label index (aliases and localized subject labels mapped to `subject_qid`; the longest whole-word label wins, a tie between different Q-ids resolves to nothing). A record with a Q-id answers only when that Q-id and its relation match (`gatedFactRecord` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_factual_qa.js`, `gated_fact_record` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/factual_qa.rs`, which now backs both `try_fact_lookup` and `fact_store_resolves`); R1172-1's word-boundary alias + keyword match survives only as the last-resort `surface_hint` for Q-id-less records (Mona Lisa, Rust creator, …). The admitting gate is logged as `fact_lookup:subject_gate:*`. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-factual-qa-subject-gate.test.mjs` (R2 cases: "capital of Canada, not the USA" is no longer answered with Washington) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_gate.rs`. The label index is still the seeded fact store, so an entity with no seeded label has no Q-id offline: the live resolution of R1172-3 remains the path for it. |
| R1172-3 | When no seeded fact's subject matches, the engine queries Wikidata live for the requested property and answers from the returned statement with its reference URL. | Implemented (JavaScript verified locally; the Rust side is drafted without a local `cargo` run, CI is its first compile): the native `fact_lookup` row is now a contextual handler (`try_fact_lookup_with_offline` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/fact_live_answer.rs`, dispatched from `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs`) that answers a seeded record first and otherwise calls `fact_live::resolve_fact_live`. The question is formalized from seed data alone (`live_fact_question`): the relation is the `fact_relation` meaning the prompt names, which must be grounded in a Wikidata property, and the subject term is the relation clause minus the relation's surfaces, the `interrogative_opener` and the `statement_function_word` words (at most four words). The answer renders the new `fact_live_answer` template of `data/seed/multilingual-responses-entities.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es) with the claim's reference URL, else the subject snapshot URL, and logs every capture. Transport is enabled only with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH` and not `offline`; otherwise committed captures replay and a miss falls through. The browser twin `resolveFactQueryViaWikidata` now answers through the same template (`factLiveSummary`, with the seed-cue extractor `factLiveQuestion` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_factual_qa.js`; the browser still routes by `parseFactQuestion`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_live_fact_answer.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-live-fact-parity.test.mjs` (fixture transports, no network). |
| R1172-4 | `fact_store_resolves` returns `false` for a prompt whose subject has no seeded record, so the open-web/live-query planner (issue #989) is not blocked by a false hit. | Implemented: `fact_store_resolves` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/benchmark_prompts.rs`) delegates to the corrected matcher, so "What is the capital of Australia?" resolves to `false` and the planner may release the prompt to the open web instead of discarding the wrong cached answer (issue #1138's regression is not reintroduced: seeded subjects still resolve `true`). Pinned by `usa_fact_no_longer_answers_australia_prompts` and `engine_no_longer_answers_australia_with_washington` in the same test file. |
| R1172-5 | Definitions ("What does X mean?") resolve via Wiktionary or Wikidata lexemes, never the canned web-search paragraph. | Implemented 2026-10-07: a definition request is answered from the registry's dictionary source before any encyclopedia or search lane, in both runtimes. The word is read through seeded frames — the `word_definition` rows of `data/seed/prompt-patterns.lino` (`what does {term} mean`, `define {term}`, `что означает {term}`, `{term} का क्या अर्थ है`, `{term}是什么意思`, `qué significa {term}`, …) — and looked up in the sources whose registry kind the same rows name (`dictionary`: Wiktionary, through the Free Dictionary entry API for English and each edition's MediaWiki extracts otherwise). Each edition's definition-section titles (`значение`, `adjetivo`/`sustantivo`/…, `शब्दसागर`), example marker (`◆`), annotation labels and inflection marker are seed rows read by one reader, so a new edition is a data change. The answer (localized `word_definition_answer`/`word_definition_sense` templates in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-concept-lookup.lino`) numbers up to three senses with their part of speech and cites the captured URL, its SHA-256 and the license. A seeded concept record still answers first; a word no dictionary capture defines falls through to the next row, which records every consulted source (#1173), so no canned paragraph is ever the answer. Native: `rust/src/solver_handlers/word_definition.rs`, the `concept_lookup` row's contextual step in `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs` (capture cache, network only with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH`); browser: `tryWordDefinition` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_concept_lookup.js`, called from `solve` before the Wikipedia lane. Pinned over committed captures (`rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1172-definitions/source-cache`, fetched 2026-10-07: en ephemeral, ru эфемерный, hi क्षणिक, es efímero, zh 苹果 with no Chinese sense) by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_word_definition.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-word-definition.test.mjs`. Wikidata lexemes are not consulted: the registry's `lexeme_api` returns no senses for the measured surfaces (its own note), so Wiktionary is the dictionary that answers. |
| R1172-6 | Comparisons ("Compare X and Y") answer with both subjects' aligned properties and the stated differences. | Implemented for seeded subjects (JavaScript verified locally; Rust twin drafted, awaiting CI): "Compare X and Y" (cues `fact_comparison_cue`, joiners `fact_comparison_joiner`, both in `data/seed/meanings-facts.lino` in en/ru/hi/zh/es) splits the prompt into two sides, resolves each through the R1172-2 label index, aligns both subjects' seeded records by relation and renders rows, differences, same-values and unaligned relations from the `fact_comparison*` templates of `data/seed/multilingual-responses-entities.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es). One seeded side and one unseeded side is the honest `fact_comparison_gap` naming the missing side; in the browser it is offered only after the research route had its turn (just before the unknown fallback), so the seeded comparison claims a prompt only when both sides resolve. Two unseeded sides ("Compare Rust and Go for writing web servers") are left alone. `tryFactComparison`/`tryFactComparisonGap` and `try_fact_comparison`; pinned by the R6 cases of both test files. Partial against the issue's wording: Wikidata-property tables and retrieved documentation for unseeded subjects still need the live path (R1172-3 / #1163). |

## Issue #1173 No Canned Search Answer in the Unknown-Reasoning Fallback

Issue [#1173](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1173) (E138)
deletes the descriptive "Web search requested for `…`" paragraph as an answer
surface and makes the unknown-reasoning fallback execute its web search. The
source analysis, the deleted answer arms, and the evidence live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1173/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1173-1 | The unknown-reasoning fallback runs the executed search for its focus and answers from the captured statements with citations; offline it answers with the existing `web_search_unavailable` response plus what the offline cache holds. | Implemented: the fallback arm in `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs` hands its focus to `answer_web_search_query`, which now executes through `execute_web_search_answer` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests/live_search.rs`) against the process source cache. Captured sources answer via issue #709 statement fusion with per-statement citations; an offline or cache-miss run still reads the cache and then degrades to the localized `web_search_unavailable` response naming the focus. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-2 | `answer_web_search_query`'s descriptive text is no longer an answer anywhere; it survives only as narration of the planned search (or is deleted). | Implemented by deletion: every `format!` arm of the old paragraph (default, latest-news, open-research; en and ru) is removed from `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`, and `try_web_search` delegates to the executed path. The provider list and fusion formula survive only as log events (`web_search:provider_planned`, `web_search:fusion_planned`) on the unavailable path — narration in the reasoning trace, never the answer. Pinned by the `no_canned_description` assertions across the same test file. |

Page-content hashes are #1184's derivation and are not claimed here. Pinned by the citation assertions in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |

## Issue #1174 Text Transforms Answered Formally

Issue [#1174](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1174) (E139,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver the text-transform family —
free-text summarization, register rewriting, grammar correction, genre
writing (Conventional Commits and business email), and sentence-level
translation — as computations over text the request itself carries, with all
recognition vocabulary and response prose in seed data and every honest
boundary (nothing to change, slot missing, word unknown) reported through a
seeded template instead of a guess. The probes, the before/after evidence,
and the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1174/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1174-1 | A summarization request that carries its own paragraph ("Summarize this paragraph: …") is answered with a weight-ranked selection of its statements under a ~30% bound (at least two, always at least one short of the input), never an echo of the source; a request that names no text is declined so the seeded-topic handlers keep it. | Delivered: `handle_summarization_request` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/summarization_request.rs` recognizes the act through the `text_summarization_action` role (surfaces in `data/seed/meanings-summarization.lino`, five languages), extracts the payload with `free_text_payload`, and runs the shared formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline (`crate::summarization`); statements under two are declined, and the selection bound can never equal the input length. |
| R1174-2 | A register-rewriting request ("Rewrite this formally: can u send me the report asap thx") substitutes every seeded informal token with its formal equivalent (casing kept), splices seeded politeness phrase rules, logs each substitution, and returns a body with no informal token; an already-formal text passes through unchanged with an honest note. | Delivered: `handle_rewrite_register` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` reads word pairs and phrase rules from `data/seed/register-lexicon.lino` (English and Russian), keeps source casing via `rebuild_core`, and answers through the `text_transform_register` response family; the no-change branch renders `text_transform_rewrite_unchanged`. |
| R1174-3 | A grammar-correction request ("Correct the grammar: She don't like apples and he have two cat.") re-agrees adjacent third-person subject + verb pairs and pluralizes a numeral's noun (irregular plurals and uncountables respected), logging each fix with the rule that fired; a clean text is reported as already grammatical. | Delivered: `handle_grammar_correction` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` applies the `subject_verb_rule`, `numeral_noun_rule`, `plural_exception` and `uncountable_noun` records of `data/seed/agreement-rules.lino` token by token; corrections render line by line through `text_transform_grammar_line` with the rule name, the body through `text_transform_grammar_result`, and the clean case through `text_transform_grammar_clean`. |
| R1174-4 | A commit-message request ("Write a commit message: correct an off-by-one error in the pagination helper") composes a Conventional Commits line from the described change — verb mapped to the seeded type, scope after the seeded preposition, effect between — and names the genre's missing slots through the incomplete template instead of fabricating them. | Delivered: the `commit_message` arm of `handle_genre_writing` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` fills the `{type}({component}): {imperative} {effect}` and no-scope templates of `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino` (styleguide URL logged); a request missing the verb or effect answers through `text_transform_genre_incomplete` at reduced confidence. |
| R1174-5 | An email request ("Write an email to my team: I am taking a day off on Friday because I am tired.") composes the seeded part frames — greeting with recipient, intent, reason after the seeded cue, weekday date, closing — in the styleguide's declared order. | Delivered: the `email` arm of `handle_genre_writing` reads the part sequence, frames, recipient preposition, possessives and reason cue from `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, resolves the weekday through the `calendar_weekday` role, and renders optional parts (reason, date) only when their cues are present. |
| R1174-6 | A translation request whose text has no quotes or backticks ("Translate to Russian: The weather is nice today, let's go for a walk.") still translates: the free sentence after the command head goes word by word through the pipeline, function words are dropped and logged, resolved words carry their meaning ids, unknown words are named through the seeded template rather than hidden, and a sentence with nothing translatable reports the honest gap. | Delivered: `translate_free_sentence` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs` (reached from `try_translation` when no quotable surface exists and source ≠ target) calls `TranslationPipeline::translate_sentence` (`rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`), which resolves each token against seeded compositional lemmas and the cache before any network request, keeps the source token order, and preserves terminal punctuation; unknown words append the `text_transform_translation_unknown` note. |
| R1174-7 | The whole family is a pure function of seed data — cues, pairs, rules, frames, and response prose live in `data/seed/` with five-language response parity — every new token the seed files introduce resolves under the total-closure audit, and no hardcoded-language or literal-predicate debt is added. | Delivered: recognition vocabulary in `register-lexicon.lino`, `agreement-rules.lino`, `writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, `meanings-summarization.lino`; responses in `multilingual-responses-text-transform.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es); the new intent keys and identifiers grounded by five-field definitions in `meanings-text-transform.lino` (registered in `data/meta/seed-registry.lino`); all six files measured net-zero unresolved under `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, and the literal-predicate count stays at its 536 ceiling. |
| R1174-8 | The family is covered by automated tests pinning each probe's intent and computed body, including the honest boundaries (no text to summarize, already formal, already grammatical, missing slots, declined prompts). | Delivered: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1174_text_transform.rs` exercises the handlers directly (the dispatch wiring belongs to the #1175 routing work delivered in the same pull request); its registration in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` and the dispatch entries are owned by the coordinating session. |
| R1174-9 | Every answer for these five classes carries its derivation as links (formalized statements, the source-language surface, the target grammar rule or style-guide clause applied) inspectable via `formal-ai explain <answer>`, per the umbrella's white-box requirement (#1183 acceptance item 2). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the handlers log their derivations as evidence-log events (`register_rewrite` per substitution, `grammar_correction` per fix with its rule, `genre_styleguide`/`genre_composition`, `summarization_statement`/`_bound`/`_selected`, and the `translation_*` steps), and the #1184 derivation record now carries them as its `rule` stage: `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino` declares each of those kinds with `collects rule`, `Derivation::record_for` (`rust/src/derivation.rs`) projects every declared kind into an `AppliedRule` (kind + detail), the record round-trips through Links Notation, and `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints them under `stage applied_rules` ("not recorded" when a route applied none). A handler joins by naming its event kind in the schema, not by a Rust edit. Pinned by `applied_rules_are_projected_round_tripped_and_explained` and `a_grammar_correction_answer_carries_its_rules_in_the_derivation` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. Since 2026-10-07 the browser worker projects the same `rule` stage for its answers (R1184-9, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_derivation.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-worker.test.mjs`). |

## Issue #1175 Routing by Formalization, Not by a Surface Word

Issue [#1175](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1175) (E140,
part of the #1183 umbrella) stops two intent detectors from claiming a prompt
because a single word matched a recognition surface: the terminal-command
detector fired whenever a prompt's first word was a seed shell token, and the
software-project detector picked its artifact kind from an artifact surface
anywhere in the prompt. The source analysis, the before/after evidence, and
the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1175/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1175-1 | The leading-token path of terminal-command detection claims a prompt only when the words after the leading shell token parse as command arguments: no question mark (ASCII or full-width), no colon followed by a space outside quotes, no bare token ending in sentence punctuation (except a token that is entirely dots — `.` and `..` are paths), and no bare function word from a small closed marker list; quoted spans are masked before every check, so prose inside quotes is data. Command shapes stay accepted, including `find . -name '*.log' -size +10M`, `make test`, `head -n 5 main.rs`, `export FOO=bar`, `touch newfile.txt`, `git commit -m 'fix the parser bug'`, and single bare tokens; the backtick+verb and verb+phrase trigger paths are unchanged. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` (`parses_as_command_arguments` with `mask_quoted_spans` and `NATURAL_LANGUAGE_MARKER_WORDS`, gated into `leading_shell_command`); JavaScript twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js` (`parsesAsCommandArguments` with `maskQuotedSpans`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-2 | The software-project handler selects its artifact kind only from the head noun of the object phrase governed by the authoring verb — the first boundary-delimited segment after the verb (benefactives and determiners skipped), or, for a verb-final (subject-object-verb) request with nothing after the verb, the last segment before it — never from an artifact word elsewhere in the prompt. Artifact-headed requests keep the frame in every lexicalised language, including unspaced CJK. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_handlers/software_project.rs` (`object_phrase_artifact` with `skip_object_phrase_lead`, `object_phrase_segments`, `boundary_cut`, `match_artifact_head`, `scan_action_from`; the old any-position `match_artifact`/`scan_match` are deleted; `software_project_claims` and `from_prompt` both route through the new analysis). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-3 | Routing is decided by a full capability-table refactor so no handler can claim on a surface match alone. | Implemented: routing is decided by the claim rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` for every handler of the precedence table; each row admits only on the structural operand its handler reads (see the 2026-10-08 last-five-rows pass below). History: Partial: this change delivers the targeted guards at the two reported detection sites and pins them with held-out probes; the wholesale capability-table refactor of every handler's claims was left open by that first pass. Re-checked 2026-10-07: still partial. New routes follow the rule without the table — the #1180 `repository_lineage` route claims only when its cue and an existing repository path are both present — but the shell-command and software-artifact rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino`, and the router consulted after formalization before the handler table, do not exist yet. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fourth pass): the router and the table now exist. The `claim` rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` (registered as a web seed) name a handler, its browser function and the structural evidence kinds that admit it: `software_project` on `object_phrase_artifact` or `approval_of_a_proposal`, `terminal_command` on `shell_command_shape` or `semantic_shell_task`, `repository_lineage` on `repository_subject`. `rust/src/capability_routing/claims.rs` (`claim_admitted`) is consulted by `meta_method_dispatch::try_dispatch` before each handler and by the solver's terminal-command fallback; `claimRouteAdmits` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_dispatch.js` is the browser twin, consulted before each synchronous handler. A handler with no row is admitted as before. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs`; `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` and the `js_misroute_ceiling` still hold. Still partial: three handlers carry rows; moving every other handler's claim into a row is what stays open. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fifth pass): nine handlers now carry rows. Six were added, each admitting on the structural operand the handler already gates on, so an admitted prompt is answered exactly as before and a row can no longer be bypassed by a later surface-word change to the handler: `page_query_text`/`tryPageQueryText` on `supplied_page` (a query line followed by the page it reads), `javascript_execution`/`tryJavaScriptExecution` on `javascript_program` (a program extractable from the prompt; the run phrase alone is refused), `incompatible_units`/`tryIncompatibleUnits` on `incompatible_unit_pair`, and the native-only `http_fetch` on `fetch_url`, `url_navigate` on `navigation_url` and `calendar_create_event` on `calendar_date_signal` (their browser twins `extractHttpFetchUrl`, `extractUrlNavigateUrl` and `mentionsCalendarCreateRequest` are bound in `CLAIM_EVIDENCE` and pinned against the same prompts). `claimRouteAdmits` now receives the handler's own normalized reading. The nine evidence kinds and the six new handler slugs are defined with five-field metadata in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino`, so the closure gap does not grow. Pinned by the extended `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (Rust awaiting CI) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (6 tests, passing); `r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` (3/3) and `issue-1175-native-lanes-snapshot.test.mjs` (9/9) still pass. Still partial, for an exact reason: the remaining handlers claim on a seed role mention or a cue list (for example `tryAdviceRequest` on the advice role, `tryRoleplayRequest` on persona triggers, `tryTrizResolution` on contradiction cues), so a row for them would either restate that surface match as evidence or need a new structural detector per handler; that per-handler detector work is the wholesale refactor that stays open. Each class needs its own structural detector (a dialogue-evidence predicate for (b), a refusal lane distinct from the claim for (a)) before its rows can be written without restating a cue. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (seventh pass): twenty-one handlers now carry rows. The numeric group, class (d) above, moved: each of its seven handlers admits on the operand its own reader parses before it answers, read by that same reader in both runtimes, so an admitted prompt is answered exactly as before. `statistics`/`tryStatistics` and `word_problem`/`tryWordProblem` admit on `stated_number` (at least one number the shared numeric reader parses: native `numeric_list::parse_numbers`, browser `parseNumericListNumbers`; Class (b), the dialogue group, reads the earlier turns — the `prior_turn:*` events of the native event log, the `history` the browser router now passes to every evidence kind — never the prompt alone: `dialogue_turn`, `prior_user_request`, `prior_reply`, `prior_software_project` (`continues_software_project` / `priorSoftwareProjectDialogue`), `prior_research_request` (`follows_research_request` / `looksLikeResearchPrompt`), `prior_procedure`, `coreference_antecedent` (`names_coreference_antecedent` / `matchingCoreferenceAntecedent`), `prior_numeric_list` (`continues_numeric_list` / `numericListHistoryContext`), `prior_program`, and the operand-or-history kinds `list_items`, `text_operation` (`parses_text_operation` / `parseTextManipulationRequest`) and `shell_command_operand`; rows: `software_project_followup`, `research_result_followup`, `research_comparison_table`, `procedural_how_to_followup`, `coreference`, `response_language_followup`, `numeric_list`, `text_manipulation`, `shell_command_transform`, `write_program_coreference`. Class (c), the composers, admit on the specification each builds from, and the seven that answer a missing specification with a named refusal take the refusal lane: `brainstorm_composition` and `creative_writing` on `composition_topic` (`topic_words` / `creativeTopicWords`), `advice_request` on `advice_topic`, `planning_request` on `cached_destination`, `regex_synthesis` on `pattern_constraints`, `sql_synthesis` on `table_reference`, `shell_command_compose` on `filesystem_object`, each with its `<handler>:refusal` event; `program_synthesis` on `function_spec`, `write_script` on `script_language`, `document_generation_plan` on `document_format`, `installation_conversion` on `install_steps`, `execution_failure` on `call_expression`, and the browser-only `write_program_concrete` and `program_blueprint_from_prompt` on `program_task`, `software_project_request` on the `software_project` evidence. Class (e), lookups and policies, admit on the subject or shape their reader extracts: `concept_lookup` and `who_is` on `concept_subject` (the concept reader or the dictionary definition frame), `definition_merge` on `definition_merge_term`, `how_it_works` on `mechanism_subject` or `prior_reply` (its no-context answer now records `how_it_works:refusal` in both runtimes and keeps it through the refusal lane), `procedural_how_to` on `procedure_task`, `web_search` on `search_focus`, `conversation_topic` on `conversation_topic_subject`, `learn_from_source` on `learnable_source`, `product_search` on `marketplace_scope`, `verifiable_task` on `verifiable_spec`, `legality_warning` on `legality_assessment`, `opinion_question` and `physical_action_question` on `assistant_addressee` (an `assistant_self_reference` surface as a word or a word with an inflectional ending of at most three letters), `punctuation_only_prompt` on `punctuation_only`, `ill_formed` on `unbalanced_brackets`, `shell_refusal` on `shell_command_shape`, `link_native_synthesis` on `stated_number`, and the browser-only `memory_program` and `memory_program_gap` on `memory_program_reading`. Natively the router is now consulted before the contextual overrides too (`meta_method_dispatch::try_dispatch`), so the rows of `concept_lookup`, `web_search`, `procedural_how_to`, `numeric_list`, `text_manipulation`, `shell_command_transform` and `response_language_followup` bind their contextual arms; in the browser `claimRouteRun` gates the synchronous table and the inline lookups of `formal_ai_worker_20.js` (`tryWhoIsQuestion`, `tryHowItWorks`, `tryWebSearch`, `tryProceduralHowTo`, `tryProceduralHowToFollowup`, `tryCoreferenceFactLookup`, `tryResponseLanguageFollowup`, `tryPunctuationOnlyPrompt`). The 38 kinds and 33 handler slugs carry five-field meaning records in `data/seed/meanings-routing-vocabulary.lino` (closure audit 1044 to 1039). Run over the 39,454 quoted prompts of `rust/tests` and the seed data, no synchronous browser handler with a row answers a prompt its row drops. Pinned by the class tests of `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` (Rust awaiting CI) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (15/15); `r1175-routing-probes` (3/3), `issue-1175-native-lanes-snapshot` (9/9), `issue-1178-creative-parity` (18/18), `issue-1177-code-tasks-parity` (12/12), `issue-1177-shell-compose-parity` (12/12), `issue-800-product-search-parity` (7/7), `issue-836-legality-warning-parity` (7/7), `issue-1085-handler-rules-parity` (5/5) and `worker-mirror` (18/18) still pass. Re-checked 2026-10-08 (last five rows): the five handlers that read nothing but their cue now read the operand their answer is about, through readers in `rust/src/capability_routing/claim_operands.rs` (`claim_operands`) and their twin `CLAIM_OPERANDS` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_claim_operands.js`; the rule interpreter gained the `value <name> operand <kind> [index]` source (Rust `ValueSource::Operand`, worker `handlerRulesResolveValues`), so a rule captures the same operand its row admits on. `docs_method_explanation` admits on `documented_method` (the prompt names the project and method of the seeded page in the `policy docs_method_explanation` block of `data/seed/handler-rules.lino`; the browser twin now runs that rule instead of an inline recognizer and a four-language answer text), `kupi_slona` on `idiom_utterance` (the idiom is the whole utterance, framed at most by the new `frame_filler_word` role and the seeded function words, so "Where can I buy an elephant figurine?" is not claimed), `source_conflict` on `attributed_alternatives` (two clauses, split at clause marks and the `clause_joiner` role, that each carry a `source_attribution_marker`; the answer names both, and a cued conflict without them, including the old "born in X or Y" disjunction, records `source_conflict:refusal` and asks for the sources), `github_repository_traffic` on `named_repository` (an owner/name slug or GitHub URL whose segments are not cue or function words, or the assistant's own repository for a `second_person_possessive`; the answer names that repository, and "my repository" without a slug answers for any repository through `github_repository_traffic:refusal` instead of naming the agent-info repository, the defect this row fixes), and `formalization_request` on `formalization_statement` (a statement beyond the cue phrases and target aliases, or a formal clause; a bare cue records `formalization_request:refusal` and answers the seeded `formalization_no_statement` response). Every handler of `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino` now carries a claim row, which both suites assert. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing_operands.rs` (held-out probes in en, ru, hi and zh; Rust awaiting CI) and the last-five-rows tests of `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs` (24/24); `issue-0918-handler-rules-batch`, `issue-1177-code-plans-parity`, `issue-1085-handler-rules-parity`, `issue-1186-formalization-parity` and `r1175-routing-probes` pass. |
| R1175-4 | A 200-prompt CI routing probe set covers every intent lane with a coverage budget, so a misroute of this class cannot land unnoticed. | Implemented 2026-10-07 for every single-turn lane: 359 held-out probes (256 en, 65 ru, 17 hi, 21 zh; 57 adversarial prose that surface-matches another lane, such as line counts over shell commands and JSON-to-YAML conversions whose keys say `lines`/`count`) in `rust/tests/fixtures/routing-probes/probes-*.lino`, each naming its lane, language and the intent the system should answer. `budget.lino` sets the coverage budget over the 105 shared lanes (every row of `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino`, every slug of `data/seed/intent-routing.lino`, plus the terminal-command detector): 85 lanes carry at least 2 probes; 20 lanes are exempt with a stated reason (10 `browser_only` memory/context rows and 10 follow-up lanes that need an earlier turn), and an exemption for a covered lane fails. The browser worker runs every probe in `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs`; the native solver (offline) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing_probes.rs`. Misroutes found while building the corpus are not fixed here: they are ratchets (`js_misroute`, 118 probes, `js_misroute_ceiling 118`; `rust_misroute unverified`, 75 probes the native answer is not yet pinned on, `rust_misroute_ceiling 75`) — a new misroute fails, a fixed browser misroute fails until its line is removed and the ceiling lowered, and the ceilings must equal the listed counts. Boundary: the native test was written without a local cargo run, so its strict set (284 probes) is confirmed by CI, not here. Re-checked 2026-10-08 (issue #1173 R1173-3): every `rust_misroute` line now names the intent the native solver answers instead — `unverified` is rejected by both corpus tests — and `the_native_solver_answers_every_probe_as_measured` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing_probes.rs` pins every probe, tolerated or not, to its fixture value and prints the corrected fixture line of each one that moved; `js_misroute_ceiling` falls to 17 and `rust_misroute_ceiling` to 39. Boundary: the 31 values that replaced `unverified` (a dropped line predicts the intended intent) were predicted from the browser twin and sibling probes without a local cargo run, so the first CI run of that test measures them. |
| R1175-5 | Three-roots parity: the browser worker's terminal detection and software-project detection follow the same rules. | Implemented 2026-10-07: the terminal-detection guard is mirrored in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js`, and the software-project guard in `detectSoftwareObjectPhrase` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_11.js`, over the shared `objectPhraseArtifact`), so the browser reads the artifact from the request's object phrase as Rust does; `ts/` is regenerated from both.
