## Issue #1176 Quantities, Dates and Statistics Computed Exactly

Issue [#1176](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1176) (E141,
part of the #1183 umbrella) replaces four classes of canned or wrong answers —
calendar offsets, statistics over stated lists, unit conversion, and
price×count word problems — with exact local computation that shows its
arithmetic. The probes, the before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1176/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1176-1 | Quantities are formalized with value and unit, the unit resolved to a Wikidata item with its conversion factor, and conversions are exact decimal arithmetic; "26.2 miles in km" → 42.1648128 km with the factor 1.609344 cited. | Implemented: `rust/src/solver_handlers/unit_conversion.rs` (browser twin `tryUnitConversion` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_units.js`) computes conversions on an exact `mantissa × 10⁻ˢᶜᵃˡᵉ` decimal (26.2 × 1.609344 = 42.1648128, 10 km → ≈6.2137119 miles, °C→°F as the formula 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 77) and the answer cites the factor it used. Re-checked 2026-10-07 — the answer-time Wikidata gap is closed: the P2370 (conversion to SI unit) capture moved from a test fixture to `data/seed/wikidata-conversion-to-si.lino`, registered for both runtimes, and is read at answer time. Each unit of a linear conversion is resolved to its Wikidata item through that capture (mile Q253276, kilometre Q828224, foot Q3710, inch Q218593, …; the SI unit a statement converts into resolves to its own item with amount 1), the factor is derived as the exact quotient of the two items' P2370 amounts (1609.344 ÷ 1000 = 1.609344), and the answer appends a localized sentence (en/ru/hi/zh/es) citing both items, the property, the capture date and the quotient; the seed factor stays only as the fallback for a unit the capture does not cover or whose amount lies past the exact decimal bounds (the ounce's 0.028349523125), and a seed factor that disagrees with the capture gives way to it and the disagreement is logged. `scripts/refresh-wikidata-conversion-to-si.mjs` re-reads every captured item through `wbgetentities` (run 2026-10-07: all 15 items match Wikidata), and `si_factors_match_the_cached_wikidata_conversion_to_si` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` still holds the SI table to the same capture. The answer path reads the capture rather than the network, so it stays deterministic and offline-safe; unit surfaces resolve to items through the seed lexicon, not through `wbsearchentities`. Unknown units (furlongs) and ambiguous lists ("5 feet 9 inches in cm") are declined. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_wikidata_grounding.rs` (English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese answers, and the uncovered ounce) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-wikidata-grounding.test.mjs`, with the mile/kilometre pins in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`. |
| R1176-2 | Word problems are formalized into quantities and relations (price × count, payment − cost) and solved, with the derivation shown (pens: 20 − 4 × 3 = 8). | Implemented: the unit-price pattern (`handle_word_problem` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs`: change 20 − 4 × 3 = 8, total 4 × 3 = 12) is joined by a general relation reading, `statistics/word_relations.rs` (twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_word_relations.js`), that folds the stated numbers by the seeded relation words of `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino` (`word_problem_gain`, `word_problem_loss`, `word_problem_group`, `word_problem_share`, with a `word_problem_question` cue, in en/ru/hi/zh/es): 5 + 3 = 8, 20 - 7 = 13, 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 6 = 4, 12 + 5 - 4 = 13, and declines numbers no relation word joins. Pinned by `relation_word_problems_derive_from_the_seeded_relation_words` and `relation_word_problems_decline_numbers_no_relation_joins` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-word-relations.test.mjs`. Relations beyond these four (rates, comparisons such as "3 more than", multi-step fractions) are not read. |
| R1176-3 | Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentile, range) are meanings with formulas in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, applied to the extracted list; mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) = 18, median = 15.5. | Implemented 2026-10-07: all seven seed-defined operations are delivered in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs` and its browser twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_statistics.js` — each a meaning with formula and source URL in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, labels localised from the seed lexemes. Mean 108 / 6 = 18 and median (15 + 16) / 2 = 15.5 are exact; the variance is the exact fraction 5460/36 rendered to seven digits with an explicit ≈ marker (the standard deviation is the one marked approximation). The percentile (`statistics_percentile`) is linear interpolation between closest ranks (the C = 1 variant, Hyndman–Fan definition 7, cited to Wikipedia): the rank stated next to the percentile word ("the 90th percentile", "90-й перцентиль", "percentil 90", "第90百分位数") leaves the dataset as a parameter, and the answer is exact with its derivation from the seed template `statistics_percentile_derivation` in five languages — 90th percentile of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: rank = 1 + (5 - 1) × 90 / 100 = 4.6; 4 + 0.6 × (5 - 4) = 4.6. A missing or out-of-range rank is declined. |
| R1176-4 | Calendar arithmetic reads the formalized offset (quantity and unit: days, weeks, months) and computes modulo the cycle: 100 days after Monday = 14 weeks + 2 days → Wednesday. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `try_calendar_reasoning` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar.rs` (twin: `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_calendar_offset.js`) reads the stated offset — numeral plus unit surface from the seed (`calendar_day`, `calendar_week`, `calendar_month`), spelled cardinals included, CJK-unspaced "100天" and "2个月" included — and shifts by it: 100 days after Monday is Wednesday with the derivation "100 days = 14 weeks + 2 days"; whole weeks state that the weekday is unchanged. Month offsets (`rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar/month.rs`): from a month name (the twelve `calendar_month_name` meanings, Wikidata Q108–Q126) they are exact modulo-12 arithmetic with the derivation shown — 5 months after November: 11 + 5 = 16 ≡ 4 (mod 12), April; from a weekday they have no single answer, because a month is no fixed number of days, so the answer is a clarification that names why and shows the day span the months can cover over a full 400-year Gregorian cycle (3 months span 89 to 92 days) and asks for the starting date. A bare "the day after X" keeps its original ±1 reading. Real-calendar date arithmetic (a dated start plus months, end-of-month clamping) is not part of this row. |
| R1176-5 | Each answer carries its derivation and all three roots answer identically. | Implemented 2026-10-07: every answer body shows the arithmetic it performed (derivation strings in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-quantities.lino`, 12 intents × 5 languages), the evidence log carries `calendar:offset`, `statistics:<op>`, `unit_conversion:<step>`, `word_problem:<role>` events, and #1184's derivation record (`derivation::finalize_answer`) completes every route. The browser worker and the TypeScript twin answer the same probes (R1176-6). |
| R1176-6 | Worker parity: the unit-conversion, statistics, word-problem and calendar-offset computations answer identically in the browser worker and the TypeScript root (pull-request follow-up row: the three-roots half of R1176-5). | Implemented 2026-10-07: unit conversion, statistics, word problems and calendar offsets have browser-worker twins that reproduce the Rust handlers' exact-decimal arithmetic and derivation text, and `ts/` is regenerated from them; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1176-statistics-parity.test.mjs` and `issue-1176-calendar-offset-parity.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1177 Code Tasks Answered Formally

Issue [#1177](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1177) (E142,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver nine code-task families —
debugging, regular-expression synthesis, SQL synthesis, shell-command
composition, code explanation, code review, test generation, code
refactoring, and JSON/YAML format conversion — as structural derivations
from seed vocabulary, with every answer stating honestly that no code,
query, command, regex or generated test was executed. The probes, the
before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1177/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1177-1 | A "find the bug / debug this" request over a function is answered by deriving the defect structurally — a binary `+`/`-` applied at top level after a division shifts the quotient and contradicts what the function name promises — with the line quoted, both fixes shown (reorder, parenthesize), and the property grounded in a source. | Implemented: `handle_code_debugging` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_debugging.rs` reads `def`/`fn`/`function` lines, resolves the name's promised property against the `function_intent` records in `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino` (each with a math source URL), and flags `sum(xs) / len(xs) - 1` as mean-minus-one with both candidate fixes; inline one-line returns are scanned too. A second defect class needs no function name: a loop bound from the seeded `index_bound_past_end` table in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino` (`range(len(xs) + 1)`, `<= len(xs)`, `<= arr.length`, `<= v.size()`, `<= v.len()`) is reported only when the same code indexes that collection, with the bound that stops one position earlier (`handler_code_debugging_reports_a_loop_bound_past_the_end`; JS twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_tasks.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`). A third class is an assignment inside a parenthesized condition that opens with a head from the seeded `assignment_in_condition` table (`if (`, `while (`). It needs a lone `=` at the condition's top level, outside quoted text, so a deliberate nested `while ((line = read()) != null)` is not reported. The fix is the comparison (`handler_code_debugging_reports_an_assignment_inside_a_condition` and its browser twin). Other defect classes fall to the honest no-defect template, which names all three covered classes. No code is executed and the answer says so. Re-checked 2026-10-07: the requirement names the shifted-quotient defect, and that derivation (line quoted, both repairs, the property grounded in the `function_intent` source) is pinned in both runtimes (`handler_code_debugging_reports_shifted_quotient` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`); the two further defect classes go beyond it, and any other class is answered by the honest no-defect template, by design rather than as an open gap. |
| R1177-2 | A regular-expression request ("five digits optionally followed by a hyphen and four digits") is composed from count, class, separator, optionality and anchor vocabulary, verified structurally, and never run against a string. | Implemented: `handle_regex_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/regex_synthesis.rs` composes from the seed word maps in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino` (number words, classes, separators, optional markers, anchor exceptions) into anchored patterns — `^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$`, `\d{3,}` for "three or more" — and `verify_structurally` rejects dangling escapes and unbalanced repetition/parens/classes before answering. Unresolvable requests are refused by name. Re-checked 2026-10-07 — the earlier "no match ever run" gap is closed in both runtimes: positive and negative examples are derived from the same constraints (the full run, the run without each optional group, a longer at-least run; a run one short, a wrong first character, one too many) and the emitted pattern text is matched against them. The native runtime has no regex engine (the `regex` crate is dev-only), so `rust/src/solver_handlers/regex_witness.rs` parses the subset the composer emits (anchors, `\d`/`\w`/`\s`, escaped literals, bracket classes, groups, `?`/`*`/`+`/`{n}`/`{n,}`/`{n,m}`) and matches with search semantics; the browser compiles the pattern with `RegExp`. Both report the same example sets and fill the answer's execution line (a pattern that disagrees with an example is reported and its confidence lowered); with no derivable example the answer says no match was run. No input of the user's is run, which is what "never run against a string" protects. Pinned by `r1177_2_regex_is_matched_against_derived_examples` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_requirement_closure.rs`, `handler_regex_synthesis_composes_anchored_pattern` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-requirement-closure.test.mjs` with `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`. |
| R1177-3 | A SQL request ("select all users older than 30") is composed into a SELECT with table, columns, WHERE filters, aggregate, ORDER BY and LIMIT — each clause mapped back to the request words that produced it — and nothing is executed against a database. | Implemented: `handle_sql_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/sql_synthesis.rs` composes the statement from seed comparatives ("older than N" → `age > N`), generic column comparisons, named filters, aggregates, "sorted by X" and "top N" cues; the answer carries a request→emission mapping row per clause and states the verification is by construction. An aggregate is grouped by the column a seeded grouping cue names (`sql_grouping` in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`: "per country", "for each department", "grouped by city", "для каждого …") — `SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY country;` with its own mapping row — and the browser twin composes the same statement (`handler_sql_synthesis_groups_an_aggregate_by_the_seeded_cue`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`). A threshold stated after the grouping becomes HAVING on the aggregate: a seeded `sql_having` cue ("having", "with", "имеющих") followed by a seeded `sql_threshold` comparator ("more than", "at least", "меньше", …) gives `SELECT customer, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;`. That span is no longer read as a WHERE filter, which before this fix emitted `WHERE with > 5`. A comparison stated before the grouping stays in WHERE (`handler_sql_synthesis_filters_groups_with_having_after_the_grouping` and its browser twin). A join is read from the seeded `sql_join` roles: the joined table is the first non-filler word after a `join` word, and the shared column the first non-filler word after a `key` word ("joined with the orders table on user_id", "соедини с таблицей orders по user_id"). It is emitted as `JOIN orders USING (user_id)`, and without a stated key no join is guessed (`handler_sql_synthesis_joins_on_a_stated_shared_column` and its browser twin). Both runtimes tokenize the lowercased prompt with edge punctuation trimmed, so `user_id` keeps its underscore whichever normalization the caller applied. Still single SELECT statements: no subqueries and no join on differently named columns. Identifying neither table nor cue refuses by name. Re-checked 2026-10-07: every clause the requirement names (table, columns, WHERE, aggregate, ORDER BY, LIMIT, each mapped to its request words, nothing executed) is composed and pinned in both runtimes (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`); subqueries and joins on differently named columns lie outside the stated single-SELECT scope. |
| R1177-4 | A file-finding request ("find .log files larger than 10 MB under /var") is composed into a shell command with a cited manual page, and not executed. | Implemented: `handle_shell_command_compose` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/shell_command_compose.rs` composes `find` with `-name` and `-size` clauses from the seed `file_context` and `size_unit` maps (MB/MiB → `M`, KB/KiB → `k`), cites the findutils manual, and marks the command Not executed. Beyond `find`, the same composer (twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_shell_compose.js`) reads four more verb families from seed cues, each flag explained from its manual page: line slices (`head`/`tail -n`, "show the last 20 lines of app.log"), content search (`grep -r`, with `-i` for an ignore-case cue and a Russian containment cue), directory listings (`ls`), and a seeded counting cue that pipes the result into `wc -l`. Pinned by `handler_shell_compose_slices_lines_and_searches_content` and the counting and Russian-grep tests in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`. A substitution request ("replace 1.0 with 2.0 in version.txt", "замени foo на bar в файле config.txt") composes `sed -i 's/1\.0/2.0/g' version.txt`. It reads seeded `substitute` / `substitute_with` role words, escapes the pattern and the replacement so they match literally, and refuses a word that holds the delimiter or a quote. Both flags are explained from the GNU sed manual record (`handler_shell_compose_composes_a_literal_sed_substitution` and its browser twin). A substitution with no file argument is not claimed. Verbs outside these families (awk, xargs pipelines, archive tools, sed scripts beyond one literal substitution) are refused by name rather than guessed. Re-checked 2026-10-07: the requirement's file-finding composition with a cited manual page and no execution is pinned in both runtimes (`engine_answers_shell_compose_request` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`); the families beyond `find` are additions, and verbs outside them are refused by name by design. |
| R1177-5 | An "explain this code" request is answered line by line: each line matched against a construct table with a grounding URL, placeholders filled from the actual code, and an overall summary of what the function name promises. | Implemented: `handle_code_explanation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_explanation.rs` (browser twin `handleCodeExplanation` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_tasks.js`) matches each line against the construct table in `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino` — def, return, division, loops, builtins, conditionals, promise chains — fills the sentence's placeholders from the line, and closes with the name-promise summary. Re-checked 2026-10-07 — the "unknown lines skipped" gap is closed: every non-blank line is now listed, a matched one with the grounding URL of its construct and an unmatched one named as left unexplained, followed by a `Coverage: m of n lines` line, so no line is silently dropped and none is guessed. Keyword-headed, closing and augmented-assignment constructs are seed rows read by one generic reader in both runtimes (`head` — comment, while, else, elif, import/from, let/var, try, except/catch, pass; `only` — a closing-brace line; `infix` — `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`), and a bare `name(args)` call has its own row, so adding a construct is a data change. No code is executed and the answer says so. Pinned by `r1177_5_every_line_is_listed_with_its_grounding_or_named_unexplained` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_requirement_closure.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-requirement-closure.test.mjs`. |
| R1177-6 | A "review this code" request reports only rule findings the code actually matches, each with severity, the quoted line, advice, and an upstream source URL — and no lint tool is run. | Implemented: `handle_code_review` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_review.rs` applies the five seed rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino` — bare `except:`, mutable default argument, `== None` instead of `is None`, `+=` string building in a loop (Python), loose `==` coercion (JavaScript) — each citing docs.python.org, PEP 8 or MDN. Language is detected from markers; a clean review says no match was found. No linter is executed and the answer says so. Re-checked 2026-10-07: the rules are data — each `rule` record carries its language, scope, `detect` and `avoid` substrings, severity, advice and source — so the reviewer reports only the rows the code matches; "no linter is run" is the requirement itself, not a gap. Pinned by `handler_code_review_reports_bare_except_with_source` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`. |
| R1177-7 | A "write tests for `f(x)`" request emits a runnable-looking pytest suite for a recognized problem shape, with expected values the shape's table states — and the suite is never executed. | Implemented: `handle_test_generation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/test_generation.rs` (browser twin `handleTestGeneration`) matches the function under test to the seed `test_cases` shapes (palindrome, average, max; trigger words are seed data), emits the cases with the expectations the shape states (`RaceCar` → true, `never odd or even` → true, `[2, 4, 6]` → 4), and adds a `normalize()` helper when case-insensitivity/space/punctuation cues are present. Re-checked 2026-10-07 — the smoke-skeleton gap is closed: each example the request states — a call followed by a seeded `test_example_relation` word ("returns", "should return", "==", "->", "возвращает", …) and a literal (number, quoted string, list, True/False/None) — becomes its own case (`square(3) returns 9` → `assert square(3) == 9`), so a function outside every shape is tested from what the request says it must return; with neither a shape nor a stated example the request is refused by name, naming the known shapes and asking for examples, instead of emitting `assert f is not None`. NOT executed, and the answer says so. Pinned by `r1177_7_stated_examples_become_cases_for_an_unknown_shape` and `r1177_7_an_unknown_shape_without_examples_is_refused_by_name` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_requirement_closure.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-requirement-closure.test.mjs`. |
| R1177-8 | A refactoring request performs the one implemented structural transformation — a JavaScript promise chain becomes an `async function` with `await`, handler bodies preserved verbatim — and refuses anything else by name. | Implemented: `handle_code_refactoring` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_refactoring.rs` parses `.then`/`.catch` chains (arrow and `function` handlers), renders each `.then` as `const <param> = await <previous>;` in order with the catch clause preserved, and states the equivalence check is structural. Promise chains are the one transformation; other refactoring targets are refused by name. No code is executed and the answer says so. Re-checked 2026-10-07: the requirement asks for exactly this one transformation and a refusal by name for the rest; both are pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs` (the browser twin additionally runs both chains against recording stubs and compares call traces). |
| R1177-9 | A JSON↔YAML conversion request converts the document, round-trips the result through the same subset parser, and compares against the input value; anything outside the subset is refused with a named reason. | Implemented: `handle_format_conversion` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/format_conversion.rs` renders a JSON `Value` to block-style YAML and parses YAML back with a subset parser (mappings, sequences, scalars); the round-trip value equality check gates the answer, and bad JSON, a failed round trip or non-subset YAML each refuse through their own seed reason template. The subset excludes anchors, multi-line literals and flow style. No file or network I/O. Re-checked 2026-10-07: conversion, the round trip through the same subset parser, the value comparison and the named refusals are pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` (`handler_format_conversion_round_trips_json_and_yaml`) and `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-format-conversion-parity.test.mjs`. Extended 2026-10-07: a CSV table converts to JSON in both runtimes (seeded `csv_to_json` cue; a header of unique non-empty names, the same field count on every row, double-quoted fields with doubled quotes). Every value stays a JSON string, since CSV carries no types, and the emitted JSON is parsed back and compared cell by cell under every header column; a table outside the CSV subset is refused through its own reason template (`r1177_9_a_csv_table_converts_to_json_and_is_checked_cell_by_cell` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_requirement_closure.rs` and its browser twin). The routing probe p119 ("Convert this CSV to JSON: …") no longer falls to the browser fallback. |
| R1177-10 | All nine families are pure functions of seed data — cues, word maps, rule tables and answer prose live in `data/seed/` — refuse unrelated prompts, and are covered by automated tests at handler and engine level. | Implemented: recognition cues and word maps are in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`, review rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino`, response templates in `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino`, and every new intent key, scope, role and package token is defined in `data/seed/meanings-code-task-templates.lino`. `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` pins all nine probes at handler and engine level (the dispatch rows are wired in `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs`), plus the refusal of unrelated prompts. All nine have browser-worker twins (`rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-format-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`), and `ts/` is regenerated from them. |
| R1177-11 | None of the nine sub-classes' answers ever recite a fetched Rosetta Code example verbatim (`rust/src/coding/rosetta_request.rs`'s `render_example` path is for the "example" intent only, not for explanation/debugging/review/etc.); the no-memorization gate (`rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`) is extended to scan the new handlers' output surfaces the same way it scans `coding-discovery-runtime.lino`. | Implemented: the no-memorization gate now scans the nine handlers' output surfaces (`CODE_TASK_OUTPUT_SURFACES` — the code-task response templates, explanation meanings, review rules, manual pages and recognition cues) with the same whole-algorithm rule it applies to `coding-discovery-runtime.lino`, generalized from `text` values to every quoted value (`code_task_output_surfaces_carry_no_whole_algorithm`), and pins that none of the nine handler sources reaches `rosetta_request` / `render_example` (`code_task_handlers_never_recite_rosetta_examples`), both in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`. |
| R1177-12 | HumanEval and MBPP are re-measured on their full upstream slices after the change and the resulting pass counts are recorded, whatever they are, in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` (consumed by `docs/status.md`'s "Latest external benchmark rows" table). | Implemented 2026-10-07, both suites recorded: the sharded dispatch (run 37613780755, fourteen 12-case windows, every case graded) measured **21/164** on the full upstream slice, up from 14/164 (2026-09-17); the row is in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` and the full-slice floor is raised to 21. Before sharding, a single job (run 37594798452) solved 89 cases in 81 minutes and was cancelled before grading; `formal-ai benchmark run --offset` and the workflow input `shard_size` split a suite into concurrent graded windows, and the total job fails unless every case was graded. MBPP (500 cases, run 37622330993, twenty-five 20-case windows, every case graded) measured **68/500** online, up from 60/500 (2026-09-18); its row is recorded and the full-slice floor is raised to 68. |

## Issue #1180 Repository History as Formal Context

Issue [#1180](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1180) (E145,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183) asks for the repository's full history —
commits, issues, pull requests, comments, reviews and Actions runs — to be
formalized into records the solver can query, so lineage questions ("which
issue asked for X and which pull request delivered it") have an answer.
R1180-1 through R1180-8 are the issue's own numbered requirements; R1180-9
through R1180-11 are derived from its "What to build", "How to test" and
"Depends on" sections so that nothing the issue asks for goes untracked. The
timeline, root causes and verification live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1180/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1180-1 | A commit importer walks `git log` on the working repository and formalizes each commit's author, committer date, subject, body, trailers (`Refs #NNN`, `Closes #NNN`, `Co-Authored-By:`) and changed paths into one record per commit. | Implemented: `rust/src/history_context/commits.rs` (`import_commits`, `formalize_commit`) records author role, committer date, subject plus body as content, every changed path as `path:` evidence, the `Refs`/`Closes` trailers as `issue:` evidence and the conversation id, and every `Co-Authored-By:` trailer (the seed's `coauthor_trailer` row in `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`, read by `coauthors` in `rust/src/history_context/items.rs`) as `coauthor:<name>` evidence. Pinned by `commit_formalization_extracts_trailers_and_changed_symbols` and `coauthor_trailers_become_evidence` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. The seed rows were silently ignored before this change because `HistoryRules::from_seed_text` did not descend under the `history_formalization` root; `rules_seed_rows_override_the_defaults` pins the fix. The importer passes its record format as `--format=` since 46d45c9e1. |
| R1180-2 | For every changed `.rs` path the importer runs `self_ast::ast_census` on the pre- and post-image blobs (`es_meta` for `.js`/`.ts`) and records which top-level items differ, not only which paths changed. | Implemented: `diff_symbols` reads both blobs with `git show` and, besides the census histogram delta, records each named top-level item that was added (+1), removed (-1) or modified (0) as `symbol:<path>#<keyword> <name>` evidence (`diff_named_items` in `rust/src/history_context/items.rs`). The item keywords (`fn struct enum trait ...` for Rust, `function class const ...` for JS/TS), the span keyword `impl` and the modifiers (`pub async export ...`) are seed rows. Pinned by `changed_items_are_recorded_by_name` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. The names come from a line-level scan of the seed's keywords, not from the AST: an item opened inside a macro or on an indented line is not named. |
| R1180-3 | An issue/PR importer reuses `github_logs`'s capture and formalizes title, body, labels, state transitions and issue↔PR/commit links. | Implemented 2026-10-07: besides title plus body, labels, the current state and the `Refs`/`Closes`/merge links, `formalize_issue_or_pull` (`rust/src/history_context/github.rs`) now records each body line that opens with the seed's requirement marker and a number as `requirement:R<n> <statement>` evidence (`requirement_statements`, `rust/src/history_context/statements.rs`; a prose reference such as `R1180-3` is not a statement), and the capture's `createdAt`/`closedAt`/`mergedAt` stamps as dated `state:<state>@<timestamp>` transitions in chronological order (`state_transitions`). The states, their timestamp fields, the marker, its leads and the evidence prefixes are the `state_transition`, `state_evidence` and `requirement_statement` rows of `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`; `formal-ai github-logs` now captures `closedAt` (issues) and `closedAt,mergedAt` (pull requests) so the transitions are dated. Pinned by `issue_bodies_formalize_into_requirement_statements_and_dated_transitions` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs` and its JS twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-statements-lineage.test.mjs`. Boundary: transitions are those the capture dates (opened, closed, merged); a reopen-then-close cycle shows only the last close, because the capture has no timeline API. |
| R1180-4 | A comments/reviews importer formalizes each comment and review as one record with author, body and timestamp, linked to its parent issue or PR. | Implemented: comment and review batches in `rust/src/history_context/github.rs` become `review` events whose conversation id is `issue-N`/`pr-N` and whose evidence names the parent; covered by `issue_and_pr_import_links_commit_to_source_issue` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-5 | A CI-run importer formalizes each Actions run (`databaseId`, `workflowName`, `conclusion`, `headSha`, `jobs`) into one record per run, carrying the failing step and error text when the run failed. | Implemented: `import_ci_runs` with `failing_step_lines` in `rust/src/history_context/github.rs`, pinned by `ci_run_import_carries_failing_steps` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-6 | Every importer is incremental from a stored cursor, and two back-to-back runs with no new history add zero records. | Implemented: `RepositoryHistoryCursor`, `import_incremental` and the id-deduplicating `write_repository_history` in `rust/src/history_context/cursor.rs`, pinned by `incremental_import_is_idempotent` and `incremental_import_only_advances_past_the_watermark` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-7 | All five record kinds are `MemoryEvent` values with `kind` in `commit / issue / pull_request / review / ci_run`, queryable through the existing memory query language with no schema change. | Implemented: the kind spellings and id prefixes are seed rows in `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`; the lineage `SELECT id FROM memory WHERE kind = 'pull_request' AND evidence LIKE '%issue:1014%'` runs through the unchanged `compile_memory_query`/`execute_memory_query` in `issue_and_pr_import_links_commit_to_source_issue` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`). |
| R1180-8 | The lineage query for `scripts/check-self-development-release.rs` returns exactly the six commits `git log --follow` lists, each with its issue and pull request. | Implemented with one caveat: `on_this_repo_check_self_development_release_lineage` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs` asserts all six commits (`88d368a5b`, `02f590106`, `96f405e0d`, `aa6a5d085`, `9efeb735c`, `33451d012`), chronological order, and `issue-1014`/`pr:1015` on the introducing commit. The issue and pull request of the five later commits are not asserted, and the test returns early on a shallow clone. |
| R1180-9 | A `formal-ai repository-history import / query` subcommand exposes the importer, following the `cli_github_logs` pattern. | Implemented: `formal-ai repository-history import` and `formal-ai repository-history query <SQL>` (`rust/src/cli_repository_history.rs`, wired in `rust/src/main.rs`) run `import_incremental` and the read-only `query_repository_history` (`rust/src/history_context/query.rs`, ANSI SQL through the unchanged memory query language). The library half is pinned by `the_repository_history_store_answers_a_query` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`; the argument parsing itself has no test. |
| R1180-10 | `formal-ai chat` answers "why does the self-development status fail?" (and the #1180 probe "what does `evaluate_calculation` do?") from the threshold, the commit range and the rule's source issue. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request, fourth pass; the engine-level answers are verified by CI, no local cargo run): the status and definition questions are now answered. Earlier the same day: the `repository_lineage` solver route (`handle_repository_lineage` in `rust/src/history_context/lineage.rs`, rank 162 in `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino`, before formalization and search) answers a lineage question about a repository path from that path's `git log --follow` history: the commits oldest first, the issue the introducing commit was made for (its trailer) and the pull request whose merge delivered it, each read through the seed's own trailer and merge patterns; an unrecorded one is said to be unrecorded. It claims only when a seeded `lineage_cue` phrase (en/ru/hi/zh/es, `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`) and a path that exists in the working repository are both present, so a cue word alone never claims (#1175). The prose is the `repository_lineage` records of `data/seed/multilingual-responses-formalization.lino` in five languages. Pinned by `lineage_subjects_need_a_cue_and_a_path`, `lineage_answer_names_the_commits_issue_and_unrecorded_pull_request` and `chat_answers_a_lineage_question_from_this_repositorys_history` (skipped on a shallow clone) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`; JS twin `js/agentic/crate/history_lineage.mjs`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-statements-lineage.test.mjs`. Still open: "why does the self-development status fail?" needs the threshold and commit range explained, not only the lineage, and "what does `evaluate_calculation` do?" needs a definition lookup (the `repository_qa` class); symbol lineage (`git log -S`) is not routed. The browser worker has no repository, so the route is native-only (an `exempt_lane` in the routing-probe budget). Fourth pass: when no lineage subject is present the route hands the prompt to `rust/src/history_context/repository_qa.rs`. A seeded `status_cue` ("self-development status" and its ru/hi/zh/es forms) is answered from the `status_rule` of `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`: the commit range from the newest `v[0-9]*` tag to HEAD (`git describe`, `git rev-list --count`) and how many of its commits carry the `Formal-AI-Session` trailer, the floor, unit and attribution and the newest release target (basis points to percent) read from `data/meta/self-hosting-ledger.lino`, and the issue that introduced `scripts/check-self-development-release.rs` (its `git log --follow` trailer, #1014); the answer says it reads the range and the ledger and does not run the measurement. A seeded `definition_cue` ("what does", "что делает", "做什么", "qué hace" …) with an identifier-shaped token the self-AST census (`data/meta/self-ast/src`) records is answered with the symbol's kind, file and line span, the first paragraph of its `///` documentation comment read from the source, and the commit that introduced it (`git log -S` over the file's extension) with that commit's issue; at most three symbols. Prose is the `repository_status_explanation` and `repository_definition*` records in five languages. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_repository_qa.rs` (including engine-level answers through `FormalAiEngine`) and the JS twin `js/agentic/crate/history_repository_qa.mjs` by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-repository-qa.test.mjs`. The `repository_lineage` claim row of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` (R1175-3) admits the route on a path, status or census-symbol subject. |
| R1180-11 | Three-roots parity: the importer is translated to the JS and TS roots. | Implemented 2026-10-08 in JavaScript (eighth pass below; all five parity tests pass locally against the census synced in 0aa1b5525). History — partial 2026-10-07: the JS root now carries the pure core (`js/agentic/crate/history_context.mjs`, including the new `stateTransitions` and `requirementStatements`), the github-logs importers (`js/agentic/crate/history_github.mjs`: `classifyLogFile`, `formalizeIssueOrPull`, `formalizeReview`, `importIssuesAndPulls`, `failingStepLines`, `importCiRuns` over `{name, text}` file entries) and the lineage route's claim and answer (`js/agentic/crate/history_lineage.mjs`), pinned by `rust/tests/web/agentic-history-context.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-statements-lineage.test.mjs`. The TS root exists: `scripts/translate-es.mjs` now renders `js/agentic/**/*.mjs` into `ts/agentic/**/*.mts` and `--check` gates it (`rust/tests/web/translate-es.test.mjs`). Still open: running git and reading/writing the store and cursor files have no JS twin, and the native `formal-ai translate` leg does not render the `.mts` set (only the JavaScript translator does). Fourth pass: the status and definition questions have a JS twin (`js/agentic/crate/history_repository_qa.mjs`: claim, census reader, documentation-comment reader and both renders; `historyRules().repositoryQa` parses the seed), with the git facts handed in, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-repository-qa.test.mjs`. Sixth pass (2026-10-07): the git subprocess, events store and cursor have a JS twin, `js/agentic/crate/history_store.mjs` over an injected io (`nodeHistoryIo` wraps `node:fs`, `node:path` and `node:child_process`): `importCommits`/`importCommitsForPath`, `mergeSubjectFor`, `writeRepositoryHistory`, the cursor read/write/advance, `repositorySlug`, `storePaths` and `importIncremental`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-store.test.mjs` against a scratch git repository (idempotent re-import, resume from the cursor). Seventh pass (2026-10-07): the JS symbol diff mirrors `diff_symbols` in full order and shape. The ES token count needed no meta-language parse after all: `es_meta::extract` is the pure `es_tokenizer` tree, whose byte-for-byte twin moved out of `scripts/translate-es.mjs` into `js/agentic/crate/es_tokenizer.mjs` (`tokenize` plus `countTokens`, the `count_tokens` twin; the script now imports it and keeps the native `Display` wording for errors), and `diffEs` emits the same `es_meta_extract token_count` change, 0 for an untokenizable side as `map_or(0)` does. `diffCensus` mirrors `diff_census` (per-kind deltas in byte order, zeros dropped, before the named items) over the optional injected `io.astCensus`. The native `formal-ai translate --from js --to ts --write` now renders the `.mts` set: `meta_translate::MODULE_SUBTREES` (`agentic`) and `SourceRoot::module_extension` map `js/agentic/**/*.mjs` to `ts/agentic/**/*.mts` in `write_target`, `translate_write::write_tree` collects them, and the rust tier of `layered-ci.yml` deletes and regenerates `.mts` with `.ts` (`the_agentic_module_subtree_writes_its_mts_twins` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_translation_tool.rs`, drafted without a local cargo run). Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-symbol-diff.test.mjs` (5 tests, passing locally). Eighth pass (2026-10-08, JavaScript verified locally): the node-kind histogram has a JS twin. meta-language's tree-sitter adapter inserts one syntax link per tree-sitter node (extras included), named exactly when the node is named, with the kind as its term, so the native census is the named-node kind count of the tree-sitter-rust parse; `js/agentic/crate/rust_ast_census.mjs` (`namedNodeHistogram`, `loadRustAstCensus`, `historyAstCensus`) takes it with the vendored web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 runtime and the tree-sitter-rust 0.24.2 release wasm — the version `rust/Cargo.lock` resolves for meta-language 0.58.2 (the npm 0.24.0 grammar differs) — under `js/vendor/tree-sitter/` (verbatim, sha256-pinned by `provenance.lino`, MIT licenses alongside, exempt from the size gate and the web precache as upstream artifacts). `node-host.mjs` `rustAstCensus` loads it and `nodeHistoryIo` accepts it as `astCensus`, so a JavaScript import records the `ast_census` delta like the default native build. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-rust-ast-census.test.mjs`: provenance and grammar-version check, exact censuses of a function and a struct, the planner histogram equal to `data/meta/self-ast.lino`, every full-AST census under `data/meta/self-ast/src` whose `content_id` matches its current source equal kind for kind (all agree once the census is the CI's own: before the sync in 0aa1b5525 the test flagged `src/agentic_coding/tool_result/command_keys.rs`, whose content id and symbol ranges had been recomputed by hand in 951b762e2 while its histogram kept the pre-edit counts), and the importer's histogram delta through `io.astCensus`. Not reproduced, and not read by the importer: the census's `total_link_count` (meta-language's token, gap and field links); the browser worker loads no tree-sitter because it imports no repository history. |

## Issue #1181 Standalone CLI Binaries and Consistent Boolean Env Switches

Issue [#1181](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1181) (E146,
part of the #1183 umbrella) has two halves: people cannot *run* the released
CLI at all (the release ships desktop apps and a VSIX but no standalone
`formal-ai` binary — the only channels are a full `cargo install` source build
or a 24.3 GB container image, #1153), and the one env switch that gates CLI
output rejects the conventional `1`/`0` spellings (`FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1
formal-ai chat …` fails with `invalid value '1' for '--silent' [possible
values: true, false]`). The evidence, the design, and the per-file change list
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Issue #1182 Duplication gates and maintained-parser adoption

| Requirement | Status | Evidence / remaining work |
|---|---|---|
| R8 In-repo duplicate-function gate | Drafted library script | Corrected lexical scanner, SHA-256 grouping, explicit baseline initialization, fresh/stale checks; fixture tests drafted. No runtime verification. |

Named-function scanning is lexical, not AST based. Rust/JavaScript closures, methods without keywords, regex literals and template interpolation need meta-language grammar integration. No Rust builds, tests, package commands or issue creation were run locally.

## Issue #1184 White-Box Derivation for Every Answer

Issue [#1184](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1184) (E148)
requires the meta algorithm to be white box: every answer carries its
derivation — search queries, fetched URLs with hashes, formalized fragments,
decomposed parts, the recomposition, the rendering, the verification — as a
durable record keyed by a content-addressed `derivation_id`, and
`formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints it afterwards. The audit of what
`EventLog`, `SourceCapture`, and `VerifiedAnswer` already provide, the plan,
and the delivery survey live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1184/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1184-1 | Every `SymbolicAnswer` the solver returns carries a `derivation_id`, content-addressed the way `VerifiedAnswer::derivation_id` is, surfaced on every calling surface. | Implemented: `SymbolicAnswer::derivation_id` computes `stable_id("answer", &answer)` from the current answer text, and its custom `Serialize` includes the id in every JSON response; `UniversalSolver` finalizes all of its return paths with a derivation link. Since 2026-10-07 every calling surface carries it: the browser worker's `finalize` result has `derivationId` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_20.js`, read by `js/app/app-conversation-hooks.jsx`), and the `/v1/responses` object of both servers has `derivation_id` (R1184-8). Pinned by `every_symbolic_answer_carries_a_stable_derivation_id`, `solver_early_returns_expose_serialized_id_and_live_record` and `the_derivation_id_is_the_same_constant_in_every_root` (`answer_91f06b150735a87e`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`, and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs` for the worker and the JS server. |
| R1184-2 | A `Derivation` record per answer captures search queries, fetches with SHA-256 and timestamps, formalized fragments, decomposed parts, recomposition, rendering, and verification evidence. | Implemented: `Derivation::record_for(log, answer_id)` projects `EventLog::events()` — `web_search:request` and both `source:http` payload spellings today; `formalize:fragment`, `decompose:part`, `recompose:bind`, `render:emit`, `verify:evidence` are named public constants the E128/E129/E131/E132 landings append. Pinned by `derivation_carries_search_queries_fetches_and_hashes_for_an_online_answer`. Re-checked 2026-10-07: every stage kind projects into its own field (`every_stage_event_kind_lands_in_its_record_field`), in both roots (`rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` replays a log carrying every stage). Which routes append each stage today: `web_search:request` and `source:http` from the online routes, `formalize:fragment` from the formalization handlers (#1186), and `render:emit` from `finalize_answer` on every answer; no route appends `decompose:part`, `recompose:bind` or `verify:evidence` yet, so those stages read `not recorded` (R1184-5) until the E129 landings append them. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |
| R1184-3 | The record is durable and queryable after the answer is returned, keyed by `derivation_id`, without replaying the request. | Implemented: `Derivation::persist`/`load` under `data/cache/derivations/<answer_id>.lino` (the `sources-registry` `cache_path` convention), lossless lino round-trip and honest miss pinned by `durable_record_round_trips_by_answer_id`; path-traversing ids are refused. Pinned by `durable_record_round_trips_by_answer_id` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`, and in the JavaScript server by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs`. |
| R1184-4 | `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints the full derivation from the durable store. | Implemented: the `Explain` subcommand in `rust/src/main.rs` backed by `rust/src/cli_explain.rs` (`--format text` readable, `--format links` the canonical record); the shared miss message names the id shape and the store path. The binary itself is pinned by `the_explain_subcommand_prints_the_durable_record` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs` (it runs `formal-ai explain` in both formats against a store in its working directory, and a miss exits non-zero naming the id); the JavaScript `node js/server/main.mjs explain` twin by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs`. |
| R1184-5 | A stage the route never populated reports "not recorded" — never fabricated or inferred. | Implemented: `explain_text` names every stage and prints `not recorded`; the lino record omits absent stages entirely. Pinned by `explain_reports_not_recorded_for_stages_a_route_did_not_populate`. Pinned by `explain_reports_not_recorded_for_stages_a_route_did_not_populate` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |
| R1184-6 | The `--thinking` trace and the derivation record are two projections of the same `EventLog`. | Implemented: `record_for` reads `EventLog::events()` and nothing else — the same log `thinking_steps_for_answer` curates. Pinned by `explain_and_thinking_trace_agree_on_the_same_event_log` (the narrated `http_chat` details are exactly the derivation's queries; the derivation additionally keeps fetch hashes the thinking view intentionally drops). Pinned by `explain_and_thinking_trace_agree_on_the_same_event_log` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |

Pinned by `explain_command_does_not_collide_with_the_self_explanation_recipe` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. |

The JavaScript server's `responseFromSymbolic` (`js/server/responses.mjs`) emits the same field in the same position. Pinned by `the_responses_api_carries_the_derivation_id_beside_evidence_links` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs`. |
| R1184-9 | Three-roots parity: `derivation` module translated to js/ts roots with cross-runtime derivation cases. | Implemented 2026-10-07 in all three roots' JavaScript surfaces (JS server and browser worker, node tests passing locally; the Rust leg of the cross-runtime case is drafted without a local cargo run). JS root: `js/agentic/crate/derivation.mjs` mirrors every pub item of `rust/src/derivation.rs` (record projection over `{kind, payload}` events in append order, both `source:http` spellings, `VerificationRecord` payload/parse, `to_lino`/`from_lino`, `explain_text`, `answer_derivation_id`, `store_path`, `miss_message`, applied rules read from the schema's `stage ... collects rule` rows of `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino`). Since 2026-10-07 `persist`, `load` and `explainAnswer` mirror `Derivation::persist`/`load` and `explain_answer` over an injected `{ readText, writeText, createDirAll }` io (the host offers no write, the convention `discovery_production.mjs` uses for the procedure cache): the file at `storePath` holds the `toLino` bytes, a record filed under another id or an unusable id is a miss, and the miss is the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text; `durable record round-trips by answer id` in the parity test pins the exact path, bytes and miss text over `node:fs`. `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` replays the Rust unit cases and pins byte-identical `to_lino` text. TS root: since 2026-10-07 `scripts/translate-es.mjs` renders it as `ts/agentic/crate/derivation.mts`. Cross-runtime case (2026-10-07): `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains `e1184_derivation_answer_id`, a prompt both solvers answer byte for byte (`DERIVATION ANSWER EVERY`); its `expectedDerivationEvidence` field is the exact `derivation:<answer id>` link, which `rust/tests/unit/specification/synthesis.rs` asserts on the Rust answer and `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` recomputes with `answerDerivationId` from the browser worker's answer (passing locally; the Rust leg is drafted without a local cargo run). JS server (2026-10-07, node tests passing locally; no Rust change): `js/server/derivation-store.mjs` mirrors `finalize_answer` on every server solve (`solveSymbolic`, so chat completions, responses, MCP and Telegram answers): it appends the `render:emit` event `answer_id=<id>;format=text` to the worker's native log, projects the record with `recordFor`, pushes `derivation:<id>`, appends `toLino` to `links_notation`, and persists under `<working directory>/data/cache/derivations/<id>.lino` (the Rust server's `std::env::current_dir`), pushing that path or `derivation:persistence_failed:<error>`. `node js/server/main.mjs explain <answer-id> [--format text|links]` mirrors `formal-ai explain` (`cli_explain::run_explain`): the canonical working directory as root, `explainText` or the stored bytes on stdout, and on a miss the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text as `Error: "…"` with exit 1. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-server.test.mjs` (persisted bytes equal the appended record, the explain request in both formats and through the CLI, the miss text, a refused write). Rust has no HTTP explain route either, so the explain request is the CLI in both runtimes. Browser worker (2026-10-07): `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_derivation.js` is the classic-script twin of the crate module (a classic worker cannot import it): `finalizeWorkerDerivation` runs `finalize_answer` on every web UI answer in the worker's `onmessage` (the `render:emit` event appended to the answer's `solverEvents`, the record projected with the schema's applied-rule kinds, `derivation:<id>` and `data/cache/derivations/<id>.lino` linked), and `explainWorkerDerivation` answers a prompt that names an `answer_<16 hex>` id and evidences the seed's `capability_act_explain` act with `explain_text`, or the stored Links Notation under `--format links`, or the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text on a miss. ## Issue #1185 Error-Driven Repair Loop

Issue [#1185](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1185) (E149)
asks the executor not to stop at the first failed step: the compiler or
runtime diagnostic in the raw failed output is formalized into structured
data, the error text is searched, a fetched source that addresses the exact
error is retained as a fix, and the failed step is retried on a bounded
ladder — with every attempt recorded as evidence and every dead end reported
honestly instead of guessed around. The audit, the seam survey, and the
worked trace live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1185/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1185-1 | The raw output of a failed build or run is formalized into a structured diagnostic — file, line, error code, message, and the raw line — through the meta language's shape table, not per-language regexes in Rust. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `formalize_diagnostic` in `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_loop.rs` runs one generic `{slot}` template matcher over the `language` records in `data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino` (14 languages), validating each slot by shape so a template cannot read prose as a path or a line number; location lines bind per the language's print order and a python traceback's innermost frame wins; absent slots stay `None`. One captured diagnostic per language formalizes to its exact file, line, code and message in `every_emitted_language_formalizes_through_the_one_shape_table` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_error_repair_loop.rs`) and in the JS root (`rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). The E128/#1163 page formalizer stays the deeper route for prose-shaped output. |
| R1185-2 | The diagnostic becomes a search query that names the language and carries the exact error code or message; the fetched pages are read, and a fragment is retained only when it addresses that exact code/message. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `search_query` composes language + error code (or a bounded message head) — pinned exactly by `the_search_query_names_the_language_and_the_exact_code`; `repair_step` plans the search, then the fetch of each unseen source URL (never refetched); `page_addresses` requires the page to carry the exact code or cover more than half the message tokens, and `fix_fragment` retains a fenced block only when its preceding window addresses the diagnostic, else the best addressing sentence. Pinned by `repair_loop_plans_the_diagnostic_search_before_any_final`, `repair_loop_records_the_fix_then_retries_the_failed_command` and `repair_loop_stops_when_no_fetched_source_matches_the_diagnostic`, with JS twins in `rust/tests/web/agentic-write.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-3 | The fix is expressed and applied in the meta language — a Links Notation `repair_edit` record written beside the artifact, never a raw text patch. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; Rust verified by CI, no local cargo run): `repair_edit_document` renders the `repair_edit` record (language, file, line, error_code, message, source URL, retained fragment, `rendering meta_language`, `applied false`) and `repair_step` writes it to `<stem>.repair.lino` beside the failing artifact, then re-runs the failed command. The apply half — rendering that record back into the target language and editing the source — was the #1167/E132 renderer's seam and is now delivered: `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_apply.rs` parses the record (`parse_repair_edit`), splices the retained fragment over the located line re-indented to that line's indentation (`splice_repair_edit`), and accepts the result only when the meta-language CST parses the whole rendered program as valid (`render_repair_edit`); a record with no retained fix, no location, a line out of range, a language the CST engine does not read, or a rendering that does not parse is refused with a named gap and never written. `repair_step` applies it (`RepairOutcome::ApplyFix`, a `write_file` of the rendered source) when the record and the artifact were both written this turn and the record is not older than the artifact, then re-runs the step. JS twin `js/agentic/repair_apply.mjs` and `applyFixPlan` in `js/agentic/repair_loop.mjs`; the JS root has no CST engine, so without a validator handed in it refuses as `unvalidated`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_repair_apply.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-repair-apply.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-4 | Retries are bounded, and the bound is reported honestly when reached. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `MAX_REPAIR_RUNGS = 3` caps the ladder; the caller owns the rung counter (a retry that fails again re-enters one rung higher), `repair_step` returns `Stop(Exhausted)` at the top, and `ladder_note` renders "rung {rung} of at most {max_rungs}" from the seed template rather than truncating silently. The executor now reports it: `plan_symbolic_command_reroute` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/command_reroute.rs`, twin `js/agentic/command_reroute.mjs`) runs `repair_step` and, on a stop, appends `stop_note` to the failure report, so a spent ladder reaches the answer. Pinned by `stop_note_reports_the_spent_ladder_and_is_silent_without_a_rung` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-stop-note.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-5 | Every attempt is recorded as an evidence chain reachable from the answer's derivation. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `attempts_from` reconstructs the chain from the transcript (diagnostic, query, candidate fix, applied, resolved) and `evidence_document` renders it as one `repair_attempts` record with `attempt_count` and one `repair_attempt` row per attempt, in the form #1184's derivation record attaches. The executor attaches it: a stopped loop's `stop_note` follows the honest note with the `repair_attempts` record in a fenced `lino` block in the final answer (Rust and JS roots), pinned by `stop_note_names_the_unresolved_need_and_carries_the_attempt_chain` and its JS twin. |
| R1185-6 | When no fetched source matches, the loop reports an unresolved need; it never fabricates a fix. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `Stop(NoMatch)` is returned when every fetched page was read and none addresses the diagnostic, `plan_repair` yields `None` so the caller falls back to today's honest failure report, and `unresolved_note` names the query and says the need is unresolved rather than guessed. The note is no longer only available: the executor appends it (with the attempt chain) to the failure report whenever the loop stops on `NoMatch`, in the request's language. |
| R1185-7 | The loop is uniform across all fourteen emitted languages. | Implemented 2026-10-07: the shape table carries all fourteen (rust, typescript, javascript, kotlin, scala, java, go, python, c, cpp, csharp, ruby, php, swift); matcher, search, retention, ladder and stops are language-agnostic, and the loop's prose renders through `localized_response`. A fourteen-language table is pinned in both roots (`every_emitted_language_formalizes_through_the_one_shape_table`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). Writing it found a PHP defect: the `{file} on line {line}` location row read the whole `PHP Parse error: … in /x.php on line 5` line as a path and dropped the diagnostic; PHP's location now sits inside its patterns (`an_inline_php_location_does_not_swallow_the_diagnostic`). |
| R1185-8 | Three-roots parity: the same loop reachable from the js and ts roots (`formal-ai translate --to js\|ts`). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the JS root `js/agentic/repair_loop.mjs` mirrors every public function of the Rust module and `js/agentic/command_reroute.mjs` drives it as the Rust executor does (`rust/tests/web/agentic-write.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-stop-note.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). The TS root is `ts/agentic/repair_loop.mts` (with every other `js/agentic` module as `.mts`), rendered by `scripts/translate-es.mjs --write` and gated by its `--check` (`rust/tests/web/translate-es.test.mjs`). Boundary: like `ts/worker`, the TS root is the canonical rendering, not separately executed; the native `formal-ai translate` leg owns only the `.js`→`.ts` set, and `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains no diagnostic cases. |

Traceability: the shape table is `data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino` with
its byte-identical embedded mirror `rust/embedded/data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino`;
the response templates are `data/seed/multilingual-responses-repair.lino` with
its byte-identical mirror `rust/embedded/data/seed/multilingual-responses-repair.lino`;
the loop is `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_loop.rs`; the probes are
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_error_repair_loop.rs` (twelve tests: rustc/kotlinc/
python-traceback formalization, no-shape refusal, search-before-final, no-match
stop, bounded ladder, non-diagnostic decline, record-then-retry, Links Notation
record, attempt-chain evidence, bounded query, planner-contract call shapes).

Wiring the main session owes (the loop is delivered inert by design, like an
unregistered cue table): `pub mod repair_loop;` in
`rust/src/agentic_coding/modules.rs`; `mod issue_1185_error_repair_loop;` in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`; the two seeds registered in
`data/meta/seed-registry.lino` (`diagnostic-code-shapes` bundle,
`multilingual-responses-repair` bundle + `lexicon response`) with the embedded
registry refreshed; and the executor hookup — the failure branch of
`plan_symbolic_command_reroute` in `rust/src/agentic_coding/command_reroute.rs`
consults `repair_loop::plan_repair` before returning `AgenticPlan::Final`,
threading a `repair_rung: u8` through `RecipeProgress`. The exact snippet is
in the module's doc comment and the case study.

## Issue #1186 Formalization as a User-Facing Task

Issue [#1186](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1186) (E150,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183): "Formalize in first-order logic: Every
student who studies passes the exam." answered with the canned web-search
paragraph on 0.347.0. The issue asks for a formalization handler that parses
a quantified sentence into a clause, renders it into first-order logic, Lean
and Rocq, deformalizes it back in en/ru/hi/zh with a structural round trip,
and does so identically in all three roots without memorizing any probe.
R1186-1 through R1186-9 are the issue's R1–R9; R1186-10 is the per-language
probe set its "Probe set and tests" section specifies. The audit and the
fix history live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1186/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1186-1 | A prompt carrying a formalization command ("formalize", "формализуй", "औपचारिक बनाओ", "形式化") routes to the formalization handler before the search fallback and never yields the canned "Web search requested" paragraph. | Implemented: the `cues` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino` declares the command surfaces per language (es too), and `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs` places `formalization_request` immediately before `product_search` and `web_search`. Pinned by `engine_answers_formalization_request` and `handler_formalizes_hindi_and_chinese_conditionals` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`, and by "the worker answers the cued formalization request" in `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs`. The surfaces live in the target seed rather than in a `formalization_command` role plus a `capability-routing.lino` route as the issue sketched. |
| R1186-2 | The handler parses a quantified sentence with a conjunction and an implication ("Every X that Ys Zs") into a nested clause, not the single-triple `SemanticStatement`. | Implemented: `parse_quantified_clause` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task.rs` builds a `QuantifiedClause` (quantifier, bound variable, antecedent predicates, consequent, optional object) from seed-declared quantifier, join, relative-marker and article words; pinned by `handler_formalizes_the_issue_probe_sentence`, `handler_formalizes_russian_conditional_in_russian` and `handler_formalizes_existential_as_conjunction` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`. `rust/src/translation/formal_statement.rs` was left as it was; the clause layer is a separate renderer. |
| R1186-3 | The clause renders to FOL with the seeded `∀`/`∃`/`∧`/`∨`/`→` symbols, matching `∀x (P(x) ∧ Q(x) → R(x))` for a two-antecedent universal conditional. | Implemented: the `fol` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`; `handler_formalizes_objectless_conditional_exactly` asserts exactly `∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x))` and `handler_formalizes_negative_quantifier` asserts `¬∃x (Cat(x) ∧ Sleeps(x) ∧ Hunts(x))` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`). |
| R1186-4 | The clause renders to Lean 4 and Rocq through the relative-meta-logic crate's export, in process, and the output compiles when `lean`/`coqc` is available; otherwise the answer says which check did not run. | Partial: Lean 4 and Rocq text is rendered from seeded templates in `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`, not by the relative-meta-logic crate (it is unpublished, link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185, and is not a dependency of `rust/Cargo.toml`). No prover is ever executed: `prover_check` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_render.rs` only looks `lean`/`coqc` up in `PATH`, and the answer states "No theorem prover was invoked" (`handler_formalizes_the_issue_probe_sentence`). The "No ..." negation bug — Lean and Rocq rendered `∃` because their conjunctive templates hardcoded it — was fixed in 2e1d6cb62 (Lean reads `{quantifier}`, Rocq gains `clause_negative` `~ (exists ...)`), pinned by `negative_quantifier_keeps_its_negation_in_lean_and_rocq` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs` and by "existential and negative readings are conjunctive" in `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs`. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fourth pass): the crate is still unpublished on crates.io and npm (#185 open), so in-process use stays impossible, but its `rml` command is now a real step. `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_rml.rs` renders a universal conditional clause as the typed fragment `rml export lean` reads (the `export_target rml` templates of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino`), runs the executable `FORMAL_AI_RML` names, else `rml` in `PATH`, and the honesty block states the outcome (`formalization_rml_absent`, `_outside_subset` for existential and negative readings, `_ran` with the exit status and Lean output path). CI checks out link-foundation/relative-meta-logic at c5513f2b958a8bd160b58c7054d408d4c446bf98 in the JS job of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-rml-export.test.mjs` runs `rml export lean` on the rendered source, asserting exit 0 and the `axiom formalized : (x : U) -> (h1 : Student x) -> …` output (exit 0 recorded locally on 2026-10-07 at that commit). JS twin `formalRmlSource`/`formalRmlCheck` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` (the browser cannot run a process, so its step is `absent`). Fifth pass (2026-10-08; JavaScript verified locally, the Rust twin drafted without a local cargo run and awaiting CI): the provers are now run. Each `prover` record of `data/seed/formal-targets.lino` (`lean` → `lean`, `.lean`; `rocq` → `coqc`, `.v`) builds a self-contained compile unit — the domain, predicate and object-constant declarations, then the rendered theorem — and when its binary is found in PATH it runs once on that unit under the temporary directory (`formal-ai-prover/clause_<FNV-1a>.<ext>`). The honesty block states the outcome in all five answer languages from seed data (`formalization_prover_none`, `_invoked`, `_absent`, `_present` in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-formalization.lino`), so "No theorem prover was invoked" appears only when none ran; the derivation's `stage=prover` fragment records each binary as `absent` or `ran:<exit>`, the exporter, and `invoked`. Rust: `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_prover.rs` (`prover_unit`, `prover_command_in`, `run_prover_with`, `prover_runs_with`, `prover_check_slots`), pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_prover_step.rs` with a stubbed PATH of stand-in `lean`/`coqc`. JavaScript: `formalProverUnit`/`formalProverChecks` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` call the `formalAiProverHost` seam, which the JavaScript server installs from `js/server/prover-host.mjs` (the browser installs none, so its provers are absent; the old hardcoded English prover sentences are gone), pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-prover-seam.test.mjs` (6 tests, stubbed PATH, passing locally). The in-process export sits behind the `ClauseExporter` seam (`seed_templates` today, recorded as `exporter` in the derivation). Re-checked 2026-10-08: link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 is still open and neither crates.io nor npm has `relative-meta-logic`, so the seam has only the seed-template exporter. Still partial for that reason alone: the Lean/Rocq text is not yet the crate's in-process export; no real `lean`/`coqc` run is recorded (neither is installed locally or in CI), so that the units compile was asserted only through the stand-ins. Since 2026-10-08 the `provers` job of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` installs Lean 4.34.1 and Rocq and runs `rust/tests/provers/issue-1186-real-provers.test.mjs`, which requires both provers in PATH and exit status 0 for the English and Russian probes; the in-process crate export stays open on relative-meta-logic#185. |
| R1186-5 | Deformalization renders FOL/Lean/Rocq back to the request language and the round trip preserves quantifier, predicates and implication, checked by re-parsing (structure, not strings). | Implemented: FOL, Lean 4, Rocq and Links Notation input all deformalize. `parse_any_formal_clause` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/formalization_task_targets.rs` reads a target back by matching it against the same seeded `formal-targets.lino` templates it was rendered from (the Links Notation field names also come from the templates), and `deformalize_answer` re-renders the parsed clause in that target and compares structure (`target_round_trip_holds`), not strings. The request language comes from the deciding cue. Pinned by `deformalization_round_trip_preserves_structure`, `deformalization_localizes_the_wrapper_prose`, `deformalization_reads_lean_rocq_and_links_notation` and `deformalization_from_lean_answers_in_the_cue_language` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs`, and for every target of all 44 probes by `every_rendered_target_deformalizes_with_its_structure_preserved` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_probe_set.rs`. The JS twin is `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-probe-set.test.mjs`. A target that does not match a seeded template (hand-written Lean with other binder names or tactics) is not read. |
| R1186-6 | `formal-ai explain <answer>` prints the derivation: parsed clause, chosen template, rendered target, and the `rml` exit status and output path when invoked. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request, fourth pass; Rust verified by CI, no local cargo run): the handler records `formalize:fragment` derivation events (the parsed clause, one per rendered target with its template, the prover lookup, and on deformalization the parsed source and the round-trip verdict), which `finalize_answer` persists under `data/cache/derivations/`, so `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints them. Pinned by `formalization_derivation_is_persisted_for_explain` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_formalization_task.rs` (it loads the record with `Derivation::load` and renders it with `explain_answer`). No `rml` step exists to report (see R1186-4), so the exit status and output path part stays open. Re-checked 2026-10-07: still partial. The relative-meta-logic crate is still unpublished, and no prover is invoked, so there is no exit status to record. Fourth pass: the rml export step of R1186-4 is recorded as a `formalize:fragment` with `stage=rml_export`, `status` (absent, outside_subset or ran), `invoked`, `command`, `exit`, `source` and `output`, so `formal-ai explain` prints the `rml` exit status and output path when it was invoked. Pinned by `the_rml_run_records_its_exit_status_and_paths` and `the_rml_step_is_a_derivation_fragment` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1186_rml_export.rs`; the real exporter's exit status is asserted by `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-rml-export.test.mjs` in CI. |
| R1186-7 | Three-roots parity: JS and TS twins of the handler, and `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains formalization cases answered identically by all three roots. | Implemented: twins exist — `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_request.js`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_formalization_targets.js` and their generated `ts/worker/` counterparts — and `rust/tests/web/issue-1186-formalization-parity.test.mjs` replays the Rust unit cases against the browser worker. `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains `e1186_formalization_first_order` (intent `formalization`, the `∀x (Student(x) ∧ Studies(x) → Passes(x, exam))` fragment, the forbidden "Web search requested" paragraph), read by `rust/tests/unit/specification/synthesis.rs` and the browser Playwright replay. Its exact-answer comparison is skipped in `synthesis.rs` because the prover-lookup sentence depends on the host's `PATH`; the fragments are compared. |
