## Issue #1187 Optional GitHub Credentials in Every Workflow

Issue [#1187](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1187) (E151,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183): tokens are "not mandatory, but optional in
all cases". One resolver chooses a GitHub App, then one `AUTOMATION_TOKEN`
secret, then `github.token`; bot pull requests get their checks by dispatch
instead of waiting for approval; isolated tests use orphan branches in this
repository; cross-repository work degrades to a report. R1187-1 through
R1187-6 are the issue's R1–R6; R1187-7 and R1187-8 are its automated and
manual tests. Existing-file migrations are deferred edits recorded in
`docs/integration-manifest.md`; the history and the #1124 check evidence
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1187/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1187-1 | Every workflow that writes to GitHub takes its token from one resolver — GitHub App (`AUTOMATION_APP_ID` + `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) → `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` → `github.token`; `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` is replaced; nothing skips or fails on a missing token; the layer is printed to the log and the job summary. | Implemented: `.github/actions/automation-token/action.yml` resolves the three layers, writes the layer to the log and `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and exposes `can-create-repositories` (true only at the App layer); `cross-org-duplication.yml`, `dependencies-latest.yml`, `e2e-isolation.yml` and now `self-authored-pull-request.yml` use it. The self-authored job no longer reads `secrets.FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN`: it passes the resolved token as `GH_TOKEN` and, for the composite action's unchanged contract, as `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` only when the layer is not `default`. `release.yml` reads no `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN`. Pinned by `the_resolver_action_implements_the_three_layers`, `no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names` and `the_self_authored_workflow_resolves_its_token_and_dispatches_checks` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs`. The action is a local mirror of link-foundation/.github `resolve-github-token` (link-foundation/.github#1), not a call to it. |
| R1187-2 | At layer `default`, the workflow that opened or pushed the pull request dispatches every `pull_request` workflow on the head commit; `layered-ci.yml`, `evidence-check.yml` and `workflows.yml` gain `workflow_dispatch` with `mode: checks`. | Implemented: `self-authored-pull-request.yml` calls `.github/actions/dispatch-checks` at layer `default` once the bot pull request exists, and the dispatcher runs `gh workflow run` on the head branch for every `pull_request` workflow that declares the checks mode. Every `pull_request` workflow now declares it (`mode` with `options: [checks]` and a `pull-request` input). Three are left out, each named with its reason in `every_pull_request_workflow_declares_the_checks_mode_or_a_reason_not_to`: `desktop-release.yml` (a dispatch publishes release assets), `external-benchmarks.yml` (a dispatch runs the credentialed full-slice jobs) and the authoring workflow itself. `release.yml` is dispatched too since its dispatch defaults to checks (R1187-3). The resolver now takes the `AUTOMATION_*` secrets as inputs from each caller. A composite action cannot read `secrets`, so it had failed to load (pinned by `the_resolver_takes_its_secrets_as_inputs_from_every_caller`). The dispatcher's own script, run against this repository's workflows with a recording `gh`, dispatches every other `pull_request` workflow in checks mode on the bot branch (`rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`); whether the dispatched runs satisfy a branch rule is part of the post-merge acceptance run (R1187-8). |
| R1187-3 | `release.yml` gets a checks-only dispatch mode that is the default, and every release, publish and tag job requires an explicit release mode and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `release.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` declares the checks-mode `mode` input (`options: [checks]`, so `actions/dispatch-checks` may dispatch it) and a `release_mode` that defaults to `checks` (`bump_type` defaults to `patch`); `manual-release`, `changelog-pr`, the Pages deploy and the release preflight's release mode each require an explicit `instant` or `changelog-pr` mode and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, and `detect-changes` names its push and pull-request triggers instead of excluding dispatch. A checks dispatch runs only the lint and test jobs. Pinned by `release_dispatch_needs_an_explicit_mode_and_main` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` and its JavaScript twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`: both parse every job of `release.yml`, take each one with a `write` permission, and require that every `||` alternative of its condition that admits `workflow_dispatch` names an explicit release mode and the main ref (a writing job with no `if:`, the preflight, must guard its own dispatch alternative the same way), that `release_mode` defaults to `checks`, and that no deferred #1187 R3 row remains in `docs/integration-manifest.md`; the manifest tolerance the rule used to have is removed. |
| R1187-4 | Workloads needing a separate test tree use an orphan branch `e2e/<purpose>/<run_id>/<name>` built with `git checkout --orphan`, an `e2e-task` issue and a pull request based on that branch, all closed and deleted at the end; a separate repository only when the resolver reports `can-create-repositories: true`; this repository's `pull_request` workflows ignore `e2e/**` bases. | Implemented: `.github/workflows/e2e-isolation.yml` builds the orphan branch from only the named paths and opens the `e2e-task` issue and the pull request. Its cleanup closes both and deletes the branches. When the resolver reports `can-create-repositories: true`, the isolated tree is pushed instead to a new private repository `<owner>/formal-ai-e2e-<run_id>`. That repository carries the tracking issue and pull request, and the cleanup deletes it. Every `pull_request` workflow carries `branches-ignore: ['e2e/**']`. Pinned in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` by `orphan_branch_isolation_needs_no_credential` and `every_pull_request_workflow_is_dispatchable_and_ignores_e2e_bases`. |
| R1187-5 | Cross-repository work opens issues directly at layer `app`/`token` when it can write there; at layer `default` it writes findings to its report and keeps one tracking issue in this repository. | Implemented: at layer `default`, `.github/workflows/cross-org-duplication.yml` drops `--open` with a `::warning::` and uploads `data/meta/cross-org-duplication.lino` as the report. It keeps one tracking issue in this repository titled "cross-org duplication findings (default credential layer)". It edits that issue while it is open and opens a new one only when none exists (job permission `issues: write`). Pinned by `cross_repository_work_keeps_one_tracking_issue_at_the_default_layer`. At layers `app` and `token`, the scan opens issues in the owning repositories through `--open`. |
| R1187-6 | `CONTRIBUTING.md` gains a "GitHub credentials" section: the three layers, `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` as the only token name, the optional GitHub App, and that nothing needs configuring. | Implemented: the "GitHub credentials" section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`, pinned by `contributing_states_the_credential_rules` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs`. The section's claim that the unit test fails on any other token secret name now holds: `no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names` rejects every `secrets.*` GitHub credential outside the `AUTOMATION_*` names. |
| R1187-7 | An automated test parses every workflow and composite action and fails on a GitHub-token secret other than the two `AUTOMATION_*` names, on a `pull_request` workflow without `workflow_dispatch`, and on a release job that can run on dispatch without an explicit mode and the `main` ref. | Implemented: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` (at that path, not under `ci_cd/` as the issue named it) parses every workflow and composite action and fails on a GitHub-token secret other than the `AUTOMATION_*` names (`no_workflow_or_action_reads_a_github_token_secret_but_the_automation_names`), on a `pull_request` workflow without `workflow_dispatch` or without the `e2e/**` ignore (`every_pull_request_workflow_is_dispatchable_and_ignores_e2e_bases`), and on a writing `release.yml` job that a dispatch can reach without an explicit mode and the `main` ref (`release_dispatch_needs_an_explicit_mode_and_main`, with no manifest exception since the R1187-3 guard was applied). The rule is checked per job and per `||` alternative, and its JavaScript twin `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs` also checks that it rejects a dispatch alternative missing either the mode or the ref. `every_pending_manifest_row_names_a_file_and_an_issue` keeps the remaining deferred rows honest. |
| R1187-8 | Manual acceptance: with no `AUTOMATION_*` configured, labelling an issue `formal-ai-solve` produces a bot pull request whose checks all start without approval, and the summary reads `layer default`. | Pending: the acceptance run itself has not happened, and it cannot happen from this branch. An `issues: labeled` event always runs the default branch's workflow file, so labelling an issue before the merge would exercise `main`'s pre-#1187 `self-authored-pull-request.yml`. The mechanism is tested now in `rust/tests/web/issue-1187-release-dispatch.test.mjs`. First, the resolver's own `resolve` script runs with every `AUTOMATION_*` input empty and writes `layer=default`, the fallback token and the summary line ``layer: `default` ``. Second, `self-authored-pull-request.yml` reacts to the `formal-ai-solve` label and calls `dispatch-checks` at layer `default` with the author's `pull-request` output. Third, the dispatcher's own `dispatch` script, run against this repository's workflows with a recording `gh`, dispatches every `pull_request` workflow except the three named exclusions with `--ref <bot branch> -f mode=checks`, `release.yml` included. What remains after the merge is one observation: label one issue `formal-ai-solve` on a repository with no `AUTOMATION_*` configured, then check that the bot pull request's checks start without an approval click and that the job summary reads `layer default`. |

## Standing Doctrine: Compiled Logic, Interfacing-Only JavaScript (2026-08-04)

Stated by the project owner as a standing architectural requirement; it
strengthens R194/R249/R380 from "as much as possible" to a boundary rule.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R536 | JavaScript must be used only as interfacing glue and for JSX (React) UI components. All logic must be compiled Rust — native on the server side, WebAssembly in the web app — and the same WASM web engine must be reused by the desktop shell and other surfaces (VS Code, etc.) rather than reimplemented. | Superseded by R995 (the 2026-09-24 three-roots doctrine below): JavaScript and TypeScript became full implementation roots, so the boundary rule no longer binds; its motivation (one logic, no divergence between surfaces) is now carried by translation through the meta language. The state recorded at supersession, kept as history: partially implemented: `js/wasm-worker/` owns the parity-sensitive primitives (about 2,156 lines of Rust) and `js/app/main.jsx` is the JSX UI; `js/worker/` still carries 35 generated `*.js` modules totalling 30,179 lines (as of 2026-09-18) of mirrored solver logic under the shrink-only ratchet `scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs`, whose per-module ceilings in `data/meta/worker-line-budget/` sum to the same figure and whose end-state target is 3,000 lines of UI glue. Desktop serves the same `js/` engine bundle and prefers the native `formal-ai serve` process; the VS Code web host runs the in-process WASM engine. The absorption epic [#658](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/658) (R380) closed with PR #691 on 2026-07-18; what remains is the measured shrink itself, enforced downward by the budget script — no tracker owns it beyond the ratchet. After absorption the JavaScript surface is capped and lint-enforced as UI/glue. |

## Standing Doctrine: JavaScript First, Full Parity, Then Translate (2026-10-06)

Stated by the project owner while continuing PR #1188 (quoted in
[the 2026-10-06 architect note](../../architect-notes/2026-10-06-javascript-first-full-parity.md)).
It sharpens the 2026-09-24 three-roots doctrine (R992-R996): JavaScript is not only a full root
but the **first** one. Requirements are implemented and tested in JavaScript
first, and Rust follows by translation through the meta language — or, until
the translator covers a construct, by a port that names its JavaScript
original. The stated reason is the same iteration speed, plus local resources:
Rust builds run in CI on push, not on the developer machine.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R997 | Every requirement of the coding, QA, reasoning and text-transform issues is implemented in the JavaScript worker before (or together with) its Rust twin; the browser handler registry carries no `null` ("native surface only") row for a handler the Rust engine has. | Delivered 2026-10-07: every handler row the Rust engine has is a JavaScript twin; `scripts/check-js-parity.mjs` measures 0 native-only rows against `js-parity-ratchet.lino` ceiling 0. The server surface follows under R1013-R1015. Beyond the handler registry, three Rust-only surfaces gained JavaScript twins on 2026-10-08: the #703 orchestration controller (`js/agentic/crate/orchestration_*.mjs`, `js/agentic/orchestration_cli.mjs`), the #563 repository summarization pipeline (`js/agentic/crate/summarization*.mjs`), and the browser worker's coding catalog, now read whole from `data/seed/hello-world-programs.lino` (R921-8); the parity gaps that remain are listed with their reasons in `docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/README.md`. |
| R998 | The number of `null` rows in the browser handler registry (`workerHandlerRegistryDefinition()` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_20.js`) only falls: `scripts/check-js-parity.mjs` fails when it exceeds the ceiling in `data/meta/js-parity-ratchet.lino`, and asks for the ceiling to be lowered when it is below. | Delivered 2026-10-06; runs in the js tier of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml`. |
| R999 | R995 is amended: a worker module's line ceiling in `data/meta/worker-line-budget/` may rise when the growth is a JavaScript twin of a native handler, and the shard's rationale names the handler keys. The budget still forbids unexplained growth. | Delivered: doctrine row, 2026-10-06, in use since — 25 budget shards cite R999 or R997-R999 for a JavaScript twin's growth. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/r999-worker-budget-rationale.test.mjs`: every worker module has a shard with a written rationale, none is above its reviewed ceiling, and every rationale that invokes the amendment names a handler key of `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino` or a function the module defines. |
| R1000 | The js → ts leg of translation runs in JavaScript (`scripts/translate-es.mjs`, a byte-for-byte twin of `rust/src/es_tokenizer.rs` + `es_meta.rs` `write_source`), so `ts/` regenerates without compiling the crate; CI proves the two translators render identical bytes. New JavaScript handler modules are written in the portable subset link-foundation/meta-language's JavaScript → Rust translator accepts (top-level functions with JSDoc types, `const`/`let`, tagged unions dispatched by `switch`, no classes, generators or destructuring) so the js → rust leg becomes mechanical when that translator is released. | js → ts twin delivered 2026-10-06 (`rust/tests/web/translate-es.test.mjs`, layered-ci ts and rust tiers). js → rust is partial, re-measured 2026-10-08: 249 of 2,369 items in scope translate, and only 24 of them are functions (the rest are constants). The output is committed as test fixtures only, so rust/src stays hand-ported and the loop is not closed until generated Rust replaces the hand twins. It runs through the upstream translator: [meta-language#196](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196) was merged on 2026-10-06 but is unreleased, so `scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs` runs `selfTranslate` from meta-language main pinned at `679a3b3c` (`data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino`; the layered-ci `js-rust` job checks out that commit). Over the 128 agentic crate and meta reasoner modules, 249 items translate and 2,120 are carried; 79 modules translate at least one item, one translates whole, and 49 are refused. Outside the scope, the planner, server and worker (233 modules) translate 819 of 6,564 items, 59 of them functions, so the scope is not widened (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/js-rust-translation-scope.md`, measured with `experiments/formal_ai_subagent/translation-scope.mjs`). Translation-friendly rewrites of the crate JavaScript (`for (let …)` loops, loops with sentinels for `.find`/`null`) were measured in sandbox copies and gained no item, so none was committed. The committed projections (`rust/tests/fixtures/js-rust-translation/`) must re-render byte for byte. All of them compile with rustc, and 72 constant and call assertions hold in the translated Rust. A module's translated count never falls, and its inferred-signature count never rises. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/js-rust-translation.test.mjs` and the `check_js_rust_translation` gate. Gaps, one upstream issue per refusal class: [meta-language#202](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/202) (sibling items, 209 carried items), [#203](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/203) (imports, 417), [#204](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/204) (`null`, 218), [#205](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/205) (JSDoc types, 210), [#206](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/206) (plain objects, 129), [#207](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/207) (closures, 99), [#208](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/208) (array methods, 324), [#209](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/209) (string methods, 183), [#210](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/210) (`new` and classes, 110), [#211](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/211) (regex and the lexer bug, 84), [#212](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/212) (statements, 62); drafts 11-13 filed as [#213](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/213)-[#215](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/215); release request for #196 on [#199](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/199#issuecomment-6055834620) (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/js-rust-translation.md`). |

## Standing Doctrine: The JavaScript Server Has Full Parity With the Rust Server (2026-10-07)

Stated by the project owner while continuing the JavaScript-first work
([the 2026-10-06 architect note](../../architect-notes/2026-10-06-javascript-first-full-parity.md),
R997-R1000): JavaScript implements everything Rust does, and that now includes
the HTTP server, with full parity with the Rust server guaranteed by CI/CD.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1013 | A dependency-free Node server (`js/server/`, entry `node js/server/main.mjs --port N`, `npm run serve:js`) serves the whole Rust HTTP surface from the browser worker: probes, `/api/hello`, `/health`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/network` and its deprecated `/v1/graph` alias, `/v1/bundle`, `/v1/links` and LinksQL, memory sync, OpenAI chat completions and Responses (with SSE), Anthropic Messages (with SSE), Gemini and Vertex, MCP, the Telegram webhook, conversation reports, every vendor-prefixed alias, the bearer and MCP-origin rules, CORS and the Rust error shapes; it takes the `formal-ai serve` flags and environment. Its modules hold no natural-language literal: the wording is `data/meta/server-messages.lino`. | Delivered 2026-10-07: `js/server/*.mjs` (each under 1000 lines) hosting the worker through `js/server/worker-host.mjs`, which the web test runtime now re-exports; `scripts/check-js-literals.mjs` holds `server_ceiling 0`; `rust/tests/web/server.test.mjs` probes every manifest route on a socket. |
| R1014 | One route table, `data/meta/server-routes.lino` (method, path or pattern, route id, auth), is the single source of truth for both servers: the JavaScript router reads it, and a Rust test holds the Rust dispatcher to it in both directions. | Delivered 2026-10-07: `js/server/routes.mjs` routes from the manifest; `rust/tests/unit/server_route_manifest.rs` asserts every manifest route is served by `handle_api_request_with_auth`, its `auth` column is the Rust bearer rule, and no method/path pair outside the manifest is served. |
| R1015 | Parity is checked, not asserted: a contract corpus covering every route (streaming, errors, auth failures, unsupported models) is sent to both servers and compared after normalizing volatile values. Protocol-shape differences (status, content type, headers, JSON field names and order, SSE frames) are never allowed; content differences are listed in a ratchet whose count only falls. | Delivered 2026-10-07: `rust/tests/fixtures/server-parity/requests.lino`, `scripts/check-server-parity.mjs`, `data/meta/server-parity-ratchet.lino`; the `server parity` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` runs it against the cached release binary. Closed 2026-10-07: the worker records the native solver's event log for every finalized turn (`solverEvents`, `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_solver_events.js`: the impulse/language prelude, the intent-formalization route from the intent table and `data/seed/handler-promotions.lino`, the calculator events with a `link-calculator` lino/step-count mirror, the write-program tail, `finalize_simple` and the meta projection) and `js/server/solver-trace.mjs` ports `EventLog::thinking_steps_for_answer`, so `thinking_steps` and `reasoning` match Rust; memory recall, memory inspection and standing requirements answer from the store ahead of the solver (`js/server/memory-answer.mjs`, `js/server/standing-requirements.mjs`); `learning_trace` and the learn route's rule proposals port `self_improvement.rs` (`js/server/self-improvement.mjs`); the consent-gated auto-free-space pass runs on import (`js/server/storage-policy.mjs`, `dreaming-*.mjs`); `DialogScope` is `withDialogScope`/`currentDialogId`; Telegram executes code through the configured execution box (`js/server/execution-box.mjs`, `telegram-execution.mjs`); floats print as serde_json does (`js/server/json.mjs`). Learned meta-reasoner chunks persist through the log as Rust's `memory_sync.rs` does: opening the store imports every `meta_learned_chunk` event into the worker, and recording an exchange appends the chunks learned since (`js/server/meta-learned.mjs`). The agentic planner is ported (`js/agentic/`, wording in `data/meta/agentic-messages.lino`), including the self-explanation and self-source-links recipes (`js/agentic/crate/self_explanation.mjs`, `js/agentic/crate/self_source_links.mjs`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/agentic-recipes-a.test.mjs`); their `round_trip_proof` counts render as Rust does without the `meta-language` feature, since no JavaScript meta-language parser exists yet. Closed 2026-10-08 (PR #1188): `js/server/solver-log.mjs` completes the worker's log in `solver.rs` order - the formalization selection and record (`js/agentic/crate/solver_formalization.mjs`, twin of `select_formalization_candidate_with_policy`, `record_formalization_selection`, `record_formalization`), the whole `IntentFormalization` record (`js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization.mjs`, with `cue_set` promotions read from `data/meta/cue-lexicon.lino`), the meta core (`js/agentic/crate/meta_frame.mjs`, `meta_core.mjs`, `method_registry.mjs`: problem frame, work units, need ledger, method registry, reasoning, upward construction, solution evidence, selection, skill ledger, the open-episode reasoning-standard audit, the obligation ledger), `search:local`, the unknown-rule `selected_rule` and the dispatching registry `method` - so the Responses `evidence_links` and the Telegram `/trace` footer project the native log (`rust/tests/web/server-solver-log.test.mjs` pins the ids the Rust server prints for the unchanged records) and `responses_*` and `telegram_message` leave the ratchet (ceiling 0; the CI `server parity` job against the branch binary is the confirmation). Open: `try_meta_discovery` answers get no meta core in the JavaScript log, and `requirement_contradiction` and rule-construction events are not mirrored; `chat_learning_trace` answers the same program and `learning_trace` but its execution status differs, because the JavaScript server has no native program-verification harness; handler-specific events of routes other than the calculator and write_program, `cue_set` conditions in the browser's own dispatch, exact memory queries (`memory_query_language.rs`), and the link-cli `.links` sidecar (a binary doublets projection rebuilt from the `.lino` log) are not mirrored. The check also gates the release: `server-parity` in `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs it on the binary `build-artifacts` built, and `auto-release`, `manual-release` and `pipeline-status` need it. |
| R1016 | No maintained source, data or document file is larger than 1500 lines (Rust keeps its stricter 1000), or it cannot be maintained. Only files nobody edits by hand are exempt: dependency lock files, verbatim captures of upstream sources, and minified bundles. Generated documents split themselves: the requirements register into an index plus parts, the changelog into recent entries plus archives. | Delivered 2026-10-07: `scripts/check-file-size.rs` measures every maintained text format at 1500 (workflows included, down from 2000); `js/app/main.jsx` became 27 modules, `js/styles.css` seven ordered stylesheets under `js/styles/`, `multilingual.spec.js` four specs, `ARCHITECTURE.md` an overview over `docs/architecture/`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` an index over `docs/requirements/assembled/`, `CHANGELOG.md` recent entries over `docs/changelog/`, and the coding-ladder results one task per line. |

## Standing Doctrine: The Recursive Meta Algorithm Is the Main Path (2026-10-06)

Stated by the project owner while continuing PR #1188 (quoted in
[the 2026-10-06 meta-algorithm architect note](../../architect-notes/2026-10-06-recursive-meta-algorithm.md)).

The system reasons about the unknown instead of recognizing known tasks. Every
word starts unknown; meanings are discovered from the request and trusted
sources, with captures pre-cached for tests. Solutions are composed and
verified, not written per task. Formal AI is put to work on real tasks of
decreasing size: the smallest failing task is made to work by discovery, then
the next bigger one.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1001 | The general loop runs on every turn ahead of the handler table, not as a fallback: it opens each request word as an unknown and grounds it without network before any handler is consulted. | Delivered 2026-10-07 in both engines: `metaReason` at the top of `solveImpl` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_20.js`) and `meta_reasoner::try_meta_answer` ahead of the handler table in `UniversalSolver` (`rust/src/solver.rs`, right after formalization, before any handler). |
| R1002 | Grounding order is request definition → learned chunk → instruction-set documentation → dictionary capture; a capture's glosses are grounded by the same function one level deeper, with depth and cycle bounds. A gloss word is looked up only when no gloss of its parent reached an operation. | Delivered: `metaGround` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_meta_reasoner.js`); `rust/tests/web/meta-reasoner.test.mjs` replays real captures. |
| R1003 | A request's own examples are its goal state: programs are enumerated over the typed instruction set shortest first, each candidate's difference is its failing examples, the first failing example is the counterexample, and parameters/thresholds are inferred from the examples. | Delivered: `formal_ai_worker_meta_synthesis.js`. |
| R1004 | The program an answer shows is the exact source the verifier (examples) or the probe (no examples) ran; an unverified program says so. | Delivered: `metaRender` + `metaVerify`; `meta_reasoned_program_unverified` intent. |
| R1005 | The instruction set, cue vocabulary, grammatical words, affixes, probes, impasse intents and response templates are seed data (`data/seed/meta-reasoning.lino`); the reasoner's code holds no natural-language literal. Operation documentation is written as the operation's reference documentation, never as a list of request words. | Delivered 2026-10-06; the trace wording moved to seed `note` records 2026-10-07, so the meta modules hold zero natural-language literals (`scripts/check-js-literals.mjs`, `meta_ceiling 0`). The rest of `js/worker` is ratcheted under R1010. |
| R1006 | A specialized handler's admission that it could not do the task (`*_skill_gap`, `*_unspecified`, `calculation_error`, `unknown`) is an impasse handed to the general loop; when nothing is derivable the answer lists the open unknowns and the question that would decide them. | Delivered: `metaResolveImpasse`. |
| R1007 | A word grounded through a source and used by a derived program is learned (a chunk keyed by the word), so a paraphrase is answered without a lookup; chunks serialise to links notation for persistence. | Delivered 2026-10-07: newly learned chunks leave each answer as an `append` memory operation of `meta_learned_chunk` records (`metaAttachLearned`), and `metaImportLearned` reads them back from the memory statements passed to `solve`; tested in `rust/tests/web/meta-reasoner.test.mjs` (recall with no lookup). The Rust server persists the same records: `SyncStore::open_at` imports every `meta_learned_chunk` event through `meta_reasoner::import_learned`, and `record_chat_exchange_with_tools` appends `take_learned()` as a `meta_learned_chunk` event (`rust/src/memory_sync.rs`; `learned_chunks_survive_the_memory_log` in `rust/tests/unit/meta_reasoner.rs`). |
| R1008 | Every answer carries its derivation in links notation (goal, unknowns with origin, program, verification, numbered events); the reasoning shown to the reader is generated from the same events. | Delivered in both engines: `result.derivationLino` in JavaScript; `meta_derivation_lino` appended to the Rust event log as `meta_derivation` by `try_meta_answer` and `resolve_impasse`. |
| R1009 | Formal AI is exercised on real tasks of decreasing size (`scripts/formal-ai-js.mjs`); each rung reached is kept in `rust/tests/fixtures/meta-reasoner/ladder.lino` and must keep being derived, never handled. | Delivered: 23 rungs, up to "Write a script that fails when any file in js/worker has more than 1000 lines" (`list_files ∘ keep_greater(read_file∘split_lines∘count_items) ∘ fail_when_any`) and "write a script that converts every file in docs/notes to upper case" (`list_files ∘ each(rewrite(upper_case))`). The file-printing program, run on a temp folder, prints exactly the files over the bound. Added 2026-10-07, each by a general rule, none by a handler: "Write a script that fails when any file in data has more than 1500 lines" (the same program, `data` bound as a location operand), "write a script that prints the files in data/seed that contain a colon" (`list_files ∘ keep_containing(read_file) ∘ print_lines`, `":"` from the colon's gloss), "replace every colon with a dash" (`replace_text` with `[":", "‒"]`, both symbols from their glosses), "remove duplicate lines and sort them" (`split_lines ∘ unique_items ∘ sort_list`, ahead of the algorithm handler's canned sort) and "write a function that returns the longest word" (`split_words ∘ maximum_by(text_length)`, the superlative of `long`, whose gloss names length). The colon, dash and longest rungs `awaits` the word's real dictionary capture: `dash` is committed; `colon` and `long` were unreachable at the API (HTTP 522/404) on 2026-10-07, so those rungs and their two tests are walked once the real captures are committed, never hand-written. |
| R1010 | The natural-language literal count in `js/worker` handler code only falls (ratchet like R998), as vocabulary and templates move to seed and handlers are replaced by derivations. | Delivered 2026-10-07: `scripts/check-js-literals.mjs` counts natural-language literals (3+ words, no code punctuation) in `js/worker/*.js` with the ts twin's tokenizer, against `data/meta/js-literal-ratchet.lino` (`worker_ceiling 1106`, `meta_ceiling 0`); above or below the ceiling fails, so the numbers only fall. Wired into the layered CI js tier. |
| R1011 | Critical blockers for general coding, attacked first: (a) a file/repository instruction set (list, read, write, run) so the loop composes repository edits; (b) a handler that claims prose it cannot parse (the arithmetic handler answering a coding request containing a number) defers to the loop; (c) multi-clause decomposition into sub-goals the loop solves one by one. | (a) Delivered: `list_files`, `read_file`, `rewrite_file` (the write combinator), `run_command`, `print_lines`, `fail_when_any` (environment node; effectful ones never serve as measures), with composed filter measures and universal quantifiers ("every file") requiring iteration. (b) Delivered: handler impasses go to the loop (R1006), and examples embedded in prose with no arrow and no artifact request are not taken as a specification. (c) Delivered: a message holding several artifact requests is decomposed into sub-goals (`metaReasonComposite`), each derived, with `subgoal` blocks in the derivation. (d) Delivered 2026-10-07, all seeded and in both engines: the bare name after a `location` cue that follows a file noun ("any file in data") is a path operand (`metaLocationOperands`, `request.rs`); a word whose dictionary gloss defines a symbol in its first sentence names that value (`metaGlossSymbol`), and values the request names bind by type, in order, to the operation that reads them (`takes`, the text-measure filter `keep_containing`, `replace_text`), with probes that hold the value; a quantifier over a value ranges over its occurrences, not a list; an imperative that opens with a documented operation and names no data asks for the procedure, and answers only when every word grounds, so a fully grounded loop wins ahead of `handleAlgorithm` / `try_algorithm` without a handler change, except after earlier turns, where a bare imperative ("Sort the results in reverse order") refines their artifact and leaves the turn to the handlers; a superlative is its stem's measure plus the seeded `degree` gloss, selected by the `maximum_by` selector (`metaGroundDegree`); and a question word (the lexicon's `interrogative_opener`) is never a term the request defines, so "What is the capital of Australia?" is no longer answered as a self-definition. |
| R1012 | The meta reasoner reaches Rust by translation (R1000) once the translator lands; until then the Rust engine's derivation and handler-impasse behavior are ported by hand, naming the JavaScript originals. | Ported by hand 2026-10-07 (`rust/src/meta_reasoner/`, every function naming its JavaScript original; `rust/tests/unit/meta_reasoner.rs` walks the same ladder). The solver runs the loop ahead of the handler table (`try_meta_answer`), runs discovery before external research when no handler took an artifact request (`try_meta_discovery`, the `metaReasonTurn` step ahead of `unknown_intent_research`), and hands handler impasses to it (`resolve_impasse`); learned chunks persist through the server memory log (R1007). Rust lookups read the committed source cache, as the JS tests replay captures. Remaining: translation (R1000) replaces the hand port. meta-language#196 has landed (unreleased; the js → rust leg pins main `679a3b3c`, `scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs`), but on 2026-10-08 it translates 1 of the 73 top-level items of the three `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_meta_*.js` modules. Imports of sibling modules, sibling calls and the constructs in upstream drafts 09-11 keep the rest carried (`data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino`, `rust/tests/web/js-rust-translation.test.mjs`), so the hand port stands. |

## Standing Doctrine: Three Roots, Full Parity, Through The Meta Language (2026-09-24)

Stated by the project owner as a standing architectural requirement (PR #1139,
issue #1138; quoted in
[the 2026-09-24 architect note](../../architect-notes/2026-09-24-three-roots-full-parity-via-the-meta-language.md)).
It supersedes the boundary rule of the 2026-08-04 doctrine above (R536):
JavaScript and TypeScript stop being interfacing-only glue and become full
implementation roots. What remains in force from R536 is its motivation — one
logic, no divergence between surfaces — now guaranteed by translation through
the meta language rather than by shrinking JavaScript out, and the reuse of the
WASM engine by surfaces that want it. The stated reason is iteration speed:
JavaScript executes faster than Rust compiles, so a js-first cycle with
mechanical translation outward shortens the loop.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R992 | Rust, JavaScript and TypeScript each fully implement the client, the backend server, and all other logic. No root is a browser-only or glue-only surface, and none is a rote copy of another: the three stay equivalent through the meta language. | Partial, re-measured 2026-10-08: `rust/` is the full implementation; `js/` carries the web app, a twin of every native handler (`data/meta/js-parity-ratchet.lino` at 0 native-only rows) and the Node server (R1013); `ts/` is generated from `js/` by `scripts/translate-es.mjs` (R1000). The js → rust leg runs through meta-language (`scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs`): part of the top-level items translate and the rest are carried by hand; `data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino` records both counts per module and only lets the translated count grow. Re-measured 2026-10-08: the committed scope is counted by that ledger, and the planner, server and worker outside it are measured, not committed, in the scope report; rust/src stays hand-ported (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/js-rust-translation-scope.md`, upstream gaps meta-language#202-#215). The migration is [plan 16](../../case-studies/issue-1138/plans/16-js-ts-rust-cycle.md). |
| R993 | Translation between any two of the four roots — rust, js, ts, meta — is available as a library function and as a script (a CLI subcommand), through the meta language as the single pivot: translate(X → Y) is extract(X → meta) then render(meta → Y), and the dispatcher holds no per-pair code. A leg that is not materialized names the plan-16 leaf that owes it rather than returning a silent no-op. | Delivered 2026-09-24 (PR #1139): `rust/src/meta_translate.rs` (library entry `formal_ai::meta_translate::translate`, `SourceRoot`, `directions()`) and `formal-ai translate --from --to [--input PATH] [--list]`. Live leg: rust → meta renders the self-AST census document. All other legs report their owing plan-16 leaf. Covered by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1138_translation_tool.rs`. |
| R994 | The development cycle may run js-first: author and test in JavaScript, translate js → ts, and translate onward into Rust through the pivot, with parity pinned by round-trip verification and path-filtered CI that gates js before ts before rust. | Documented in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) Development Workflow (2026-09-24). The path-filtered CI leg is plan 16 L4 and the CST-equal round trip is L5; both pending, so today the cycle is stated direction plus the R993 dispatcher, not yet a closed loop. The js → rust step exists since 2026-10-08: meta-language self-translation (main `679a3b3c`, unreleased) translates 249 of 2,369 items of the 128 agentic crate and meta reasoner modules (24 functions, the rest constants; re-measured 2026-10-08). The layered-ci `js-rust` job, which runs after js, re-renders and compiles them (`scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs`, `rust/tests/web/js-rust-translation.test.mjs`). The translated Rust does not yet replace hand-written Rust, so the loop stays open. Most carried items are blocked by upstream gaps, filed one per refusal class as meta-language#202-#212; the largest are imports ([#203](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/203)), array methods ([#208](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/208)), `null` ([#204](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/204)) and calls of sibling items ([#202](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/202)). A release with #196 is requested on [#199](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/199#issuecomment-6055834620) (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/js-rust-translation-scope.md`). |
| R995 | The 2026-08-04 interfacing-only-JavaScript boundary (R536) is superseded as stated above; the worker shrink ratchet `scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs` stays in force as downward pressure on the generated mirror until the parity migration replaces those modules, after which its 3,000-line end-state dissolves rather than being met. | Delivered, re-checked 2026-10-08: R536's row now records its supersession by this row (its text kept as history), and the worker shrink ratchet stays a required gate — the lint job runs `scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs` over the per-module ceilings in `data/meta/worker-line-budget/` (pinned by `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/release_publishing.rs`), amended by R999 for JavaScript twins (pinned by `rust/tests/web/r999-worker-budget-rationale.test.mjs`). |
| R996 | The parity state is reported honestly wherever it is claimed: rust complete, js partial (web app plus generated mirror under ratchet), ts a stub, until each leg lands; no document may claim full three-root parity ahead of the measured migration. | Delivered, re-checked 2026-10-08. `docs/source-roots.md` now states the measured per-root state — rust the full implementation, js with every native handler twinned (0 native-only rows) and the Node server still partial (R1013), ts generated from js since R1000 — and `rust/tests/web/r996-parity-reporting.test.mjs` holds each of its claims to the thing it describes (the ts row to what `ts/` holds, the js count to `data/meta/js-parity-ratchet.lino`, no root but rust called the full implementation). |

## Standing Doctrine: Work Is Delegated to Formal AI Itself (2026-10-07)

Stated by the project owner while continuing PR #1188: "keep delegating to
Formal AI itself some work, so at least it will be able to do smallest
possible tasks just fine, by generalization and discovery with caching, not by
hardcoding. As human programmer would traditionally do if learning something
new." It extends the task ladder of the recursive meta algorithm
([R1009](../doctrine-standing-doctrine-recursive-meta-algorithm-2026-10-06.md)).

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1017 | Development work keeps being put to Formal AI itself: the small real tasks met while building the system (scripts over the repository's own files, text edits, list and word programs) are asked of `scripts/formal-ai-js.mjs` first. A task it cannot derive becomes a ladder rung, and it is made to work only by a general mechanism — a seeded cue, affix or documented operation, a gloss-grounding rule, a cached dictionary capture — never by a handler or rule written for that request. | Delivered as a standing practice, re-checked 2026-10-08: five tasks from this pull request's own work were put to it (a bare directory operand, a symbol named by a word, symbol replacement, duplicate removal plus sorting claimed by the `algorithm` handler, a superlative) and now derive as ladder rungs in `rust/tests/fixtures/meta-reasoner/ladder.lino` (the folder-scan scripts, `replace every colon with a dash`, `remove duplicate lines and sort them`, `write a function that returns the longest word`); `rust/tests/web/meta-reasoner.test.mjs` (*every rung of the task ladder is derived, never handled*, 13/13) runs every rung through `scripts/formal-ai-js.mjs`'s runtime and fails on any rung answered by a handler. A sixth, "Reverse the order of words", failed while "reverse the words" worked; the English `reverse_words` row of `data/seed/operation-vocabulary.lino` gained the `reverse+words` token combo the other languages already carry, pinned by `rust/tests/web/r1017-delegated-tasks.test.mjs`. Counting questions ("How many words/lines/characters/unique words are in '...'?", "How many lines start with x in ...", "Keep only the lines that start with x: ...", "Count the vowels in 'formal'") now derive in both runtimes from seed data — a `counting_cue` block and per-operation `unit` nouns asked of the request's framing outside its quoted payload, a `filter_lines_by_prefix` row whose phrase carries its argument, and `members` on the seeded `vowels` class — pinned by `rust/tests/web/r1017-counting-tasks.test.mjs`. Four more families derive from seeded meanings rather than misrouting: the weekday of a stated date (`calendar_weekday_query`, a day count from 1970-01-01, impossible dates declined), primality by trial division with a factor for composites (`number_property_prime`), a spelled function call ("the square root of 144" read through `math_function_name` and the `math_function_argument_marker` role into `sqrt(144)`), and a sort or reverse request with no language named answered with the sorted list itself; pinned by `rust/tests/web/r1017-small-math-tasks.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/unit/r1017_small_math_tasks.rs`. |
| R1026 | What the coding agents produce while working on Formal AI and want to keep (probe tools, the gaps found by probing, task prompts, claims, sandboxes) lives in the repository's `experiments/` folder rather than a private scratchpad, so Formal AI can read, edit and run it when asked and works as a subagent on its own requirements, and the recursive self-improvement arrives faster. (Owner, 2026-10-08: "Try use experiments folders in our repository instead of scratchpad for everything that is useful, Formal AI may use them too, if asked.") | Implemented 2026-10-08: `experiments/formal_ai_subagent/` holds the shared preamble, the claims, the gap list (`gaps.md`), the bulk task prompts (`tasks/`), the planner probe (`probe.mjs`) and git-ignored sandboxes, with the loop written up in its `README.md`. ## Standing Doctrine: Workstation Resources and Continuous Delivery (2026-10-07)

Recovered from the owner's directives while continuing PR #1188
(`experiments/issue_1138_feedback_recovery/recovered-2026-10-07.md`) and
diffed against the register: these were stated but not yet recorded. They
govern how work is done on the owner's workstation and when a pull request
counts as finished, alongside the work-in-bulk rule of CONTRIBUTING.md and the
delegation doctrine of
[R1017](../doctrine-standing-doctrine-work-delegated-to-formal-ai-2026-10-07.md).

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1018 | Local verification runs a single test (one test file) at a time, never a parallel suite: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>` and the serialized `npm run test:web`. When the workstation's CPU is overloaded by test processes, the owner's processes are never killed; the root cause (unbounded test concurrency, a runaway runner) is fixed instead. (Owner, 2026-10-06 21:18/21:19.) | Implemented: `npm run test:web` runs `node --test --test-concurrency=1` (package.json), and CONTRIBUTING "Work in bulk; verify selectively" now states the single-test rule and the never-kill rule; every sub-agent brief of PR #1188 carried the `while pgrep -f "^node --test"` serialization guard. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`local_verification_runs_one_test_file_at_a_time`). |
| R1019 | No more than two or three sub-agents run at once, chosen with the workstation's disk, RAM and CPU in mind; every sub-agent is told the same limits. Sub-agents only make code changes; they run the JavaScript Formal AI only when absolutely necessary and never run builds or full suites, because CI/CD checks everything. (Owner, 2026-10-06 20:17/20:32.) | Implemented as a process rule: CONTRIBUTING "Delegate to Opus sub-agents only" now names the two-to-three cap, the shared resource limits and the code-changes-only scope; PR #1188's case study (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/`) records the cap being kept. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`sub_agents_are_capped_and_make_code_changes_only`). |
| R1020 | Rust is never built locally to check a change: a Rust build or test is triggered by pushing, and CI/CD is the Rust verifier. Artifacts that need a Rust build (the WASM worker, `ts/` translation) are produced by CI or by a JavaScript twin. (Owner, 2026-10-06 13:17: "minimize rust building or delegate it fully to CI/CD (meaning to trigger Rust builds we just do push)".) | Implemented as a process rule: CONTRIBUTING "Work in bulk" states that Rust is verified by pushing; the WASM worker is refreshed from the CI-built `formal-ai-worker-wasm` artifact the release workflow uploads (`.github/workflows/release.yml`), and `ts/` is produced by the JavaScript twin `scripts/translate-es.mjs`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`rust_is_verified_by_pushing_and_its_artifacts_come_from_ci`). |
| R1021 | The requirement status recorded in the repository is kept current while a pull request is worked on: each batch that changes what is delivered updates the owning requirement rows and regenerates the assembled register in the same push, rather than at the end. (Owner, 2026-10-06 20:08: "continue to recheck and update status of requirements in the repository".) | Implemented: each batch of PR #1188 regenerates the assembled register and the requirement-status ledger (`scripts/assemble-requirements.rs`, `scripts/generate-requirement-status.rs`, `scripts/render-status.rs`) in the same push, and `rust-script scripts/check-requirement-status.rs` gates the parity. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`requirement_status_is_regenerated_with_each_batch_and_gated`). |
| R1022 | Work on a pull request does not idle-wait: while CI runs, the agent re-reads the requirements, the pull request and the code and re-verifies each planned requirement; it stops only when every planned requirement is delivered, CI/CD is green, and the release is guaranteed deliverable. (Owner, 2026-10-06 17:00, 18:36, 18:52; 2026-10-07 05:32, 05:36: "Why waiting again? Did you check that everything is fully done?") | Implemented as a process rule in CONTRIBUTING "Work in bulk": while CI runs, the agent keeps drafting the open requirement rows; the PR #1188 case study records the rows drafted during CI waits. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`work_does_not_idle_on_ci_or_put_choices_to_the_owner`). |
| R1023 | Open technical choices are decided by the agent from the best available practices (researched online when needed), not put to the owner as questions. (Owner, 2026-10-06 18:54: "don't ask me questions, figure it out yourself ... based on best available practices in the internet".) | Implemented as a process rule in CONTRIBUTING "Work in bulk" ("Decide, don't ask"). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/doctrine_2026_10_07.rs` (`work_does_not_idle_on_ci_or_put_choices_to_the_owner`). |
